## Barry fixtures

Repositories generated with Barry, and what a correct validator must conclude from each.

### M0

#### `m0-minimal-valid`: Minimal valid repository: TA, one CA, one ROA

The smallest repository that exercises a full chain: a trust anchor that
certifies one CA, which issues one ROA. Each publication point has the CRL
and manifest Barry generates. Only the TA's serial number is overridden
(Barry gives it 0, F-029), so every object is correct.

In M0 it proves the fixture pipeline works end to end: descriptor,
generation, metadata check, catalog and test helper. In later milestones
it is the positive baseline: every stage of the validator must accept it
and produce exactly one VRP. Invalid fixtures should differ from it in
one field, so a rejection can be traced to that one change.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2)), [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [6487 §4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4)), [9286 §4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4)), [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4))

### M1

#### `m1-cert-no-ski`: CA certificate without a Subject Key Identifier

The baseline tree with one change: the CA certificate has no Subject Key
Identifier extension. RFC 6487 section 4.8.2 says it MUST appear in all
resource certificates; it is also how children find their issuer (AKI),
so validation must reject the certificate.

In M1 it checks that a missing mandatory extension is not a decoding
error: the certificate decodes and simply has no SKI.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ta/ca1.cer`: no Subject Key Identifier; RFC 6487 section 4.8.2 requires it
- **RFC:** [6487 §4.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.2)), [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)), [8897 §3.1](../rfc/rfc8897.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8897.html#section-3.1))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-no-ski/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-no-ski/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-no-ski/rsync)

#### `m1-cert-unknown-critical-extension`: CA certificate with an unrecognized critical extension

The baseline tree with one change: the CA certificate carries an extra,
critical extension with an OID no validator knows (1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.1).
RFC 6487 section 4.8 says a certificate-using system MUST reject a
certificate with a critical extension it does not recognize.

The extension is critical on purpose: for an unknown non-critical
extension the RFCs allow either ignoring or rejecting it (F-015 in
doc/rfc-findings.md), so that case is left for M4.

In M1 it checks that unknown extensions are kept, with their criticality,
instead of being dropped or failing the decode.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ta/ca1.cer`: unrecognized critical extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.1; RFC 6487 section 4.8
- **RFC:** [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)), [5280 §4.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.2))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-unknown-critical-extension/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-unknown-critical-extension/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-unknown-critical-extension/rsync)

#### `m1-cert-version-2`: CA certificate with X.509 version 2

The baseline tree with one change: the CA certificate's version field is
1, meaning X.509 v2. RFC 6487 section 4.1 requires version 3, and RFC 8897
section 3.1 requires relying parties to check the profile, so validation
must reject it.

In M1 it checks that decoding is structural: the certificate must still
decode, with version 2 visible, so that M4 can reject it with a precise
reason instead of a generic decode error.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ta/ca1.cer`: version is 2; RFC 6487 section 4.1 requires version 3
- **RFC:** [6487 §4.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.1)), [8897 §3.1](../rfc/rfc8897.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8897.html#section-3.1)), [5280 §4.1.2.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.1))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-version-2/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-version-2/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-version-2/rsync)

#### `m1-resources-inherit`: CA certificate that inherits all its resources

A three-level tree, TA -> ca1 -> ca2, where ca2's IP address blocks (IPv4
and IPv6) and AS numbers are all "inherit". By RFC 3779 the actual
resources come from the issuer, ca1, and the certificate is valid.

In M1 it checks that inherit is decoded as its own value (:inherit), not
as an empty resource list, for both extensions. M6 reuses it for
resource inclusion, where inherit must resolve up the chain.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [3779 §3.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.3)), [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)), [6487 §4.8.11](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.11))

#### `m1-roa-prefixes`: ROA with IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes, with and without maxLength

A valid ROA for AS64496 with three prefixes: 1.1.0.0/17 with maxLength
24, 1.1.128.0/24 without maxLength, and 0101::/16 with maxLength 48. All
lie inside the EE certificate's resources and are in canonical order.

It checks that ROA decoding handles both address families, keeps an
absent maxLength distinct from a present one, and turns each address
into the right VRP: the maximum length is the prefix length when
maxLength is absent. M7 reuses it as a positive case producing exactly
these three VRPs.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [9582 §4.3](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3)), [9582 §4.3.2.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.1)), [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)), [9582 §4.3.3](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.3))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-roa-prefixes/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-roa-prefixes/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-roa-prefixes/rsync)

#### `m1-roa-version-2`: ROA with version 2

The baseline tree with one change: the ROA's version is 2. RFC 9582
section 4.1 says it MUST be 0, so validation must reject the ROA. This is
the incorrect repository from Barry's own tutorial.

In M1 it checks that the decoder doesn't treat the wrong version as a
decoding error: the ROA decodes with version 2 visible, and the version
is explicitly encoded (it isn't the DEFAULT), so the object is still DER.

ROA content validation (#171): the ROA is invalid, rule roa_version.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ca1/roa1.roa`: version is 2; RFC 9582 section 4.1 requires 0
- **RFC:** [9582 §4.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.1))

### M2

#### `m2-ta-empty-ip`: Trust anchor certificate with an empty IP resource extension

A TA certificate whose IP Address Delegation extension is present but
empty: an IPAddrBlocks with no address families. Its AS resources are
normal. RFC 8630 section 2.3 requires the TA's INR extension(s) to
contain a non-empty set of resources.

Whether "a non-empty set" means the union of both extensions or each
extension is ambiguous (F-023 in doc/rfc-findings.md). Lumina reads it as
each present extension, so this TA is rejected even though its AS set
is not empty.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ta.cer`: the IP resource extension is empty; RFC 8630 section 2.3
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)), [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m2-ta-empty-ip/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m2-ta-empty-ip/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m2-ta-empty-ip/rsync)

#### `m2-ta-inherit`: Trust anchor certificate that inherits its IP resources

A TA certificate whose IP Address Delegation extension uses "inherit"
for both address families. RFC 8630 section 2.3 says the TA's INR
extensions MUST NOT use the inherit form: a self-signed certificate has
no issuer to inherit from. The TA, and so everything under it, must be
rejected.

It checks that the TA check looks at the resources and not just the key:
the TAL key matches this certificate exactly.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ta.cer`: IP resources are inherit; RFC 8630 section 2.3 forbids it in a TA
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m2-ta-inherit/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m2-ta-inherit/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m2-ta-inherit/rsync)

#### `m2-ta-not-ca`: Trust anchor certificate that is not a CA (cA = false)

A TA certificate whose Basic Constraints say cA = false. RFC 8630
section 2.3 requires the TA to be a self-signed CA certificate; a
certificate that isn't a CA can't issue the rest of the tree, whatever
key it carries.

The key matches the TAL exactly, so only the CA check catches it.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ta.cer`: Basic Constraints cA is false; RFC 8630 section 2.3 requires a CA certificate
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)), [6487 §4.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.1))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m2-ta-not-ca/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m2-ta-not-ca/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m2-ta-not-ca/rsync)

### M3

#### `m3-walk-deep`: A chain of four CAs below the TA

TA, ca1, ca2, ca3, ca4 and a ROA: five publication points, depths 0 to 4.
RFC 6481 §5 says the walk SHOULD support a locally configured maximum
chain length (D-008: 32 by default). With a test-sized limit of 2 the
walk must stop before ca3 and report it; with the default it must reach
ca4.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-deep/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-deep/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-deep/rsync)

#### `m3-walk-delegation`: A CA whose publication point is on a second rsync host

The TA certifies two CAs. ca1 publishes beside the TA, on the same host;
ca2's caRepository is on another host, rsync://other.example:8873/repo/ca2.
This is how LACNIC delegates to registro.br and to an Amazon-hosted
directory. The walk must fetch ca2's publication point from the host its
certificate names, as its own rsync run, and not from the TA's host
(D-009). Its files are generated under rsync/other/, which tests serve
from a second daemon.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [6487 §4.8.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.1))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-delegation/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-delegation/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-delegation/rsync)

#### `m3-walk-loop`: A CA that names its parent's publication point as its own

ca2 is issued by ca1 and published in ca1's directory, and its
caRepository is that same directory. Walking ca2 leads back to the
publication point that holds ca2.cer, so a naive walk never ends. The
walk must notice that the publication point belongs to an ancestor,
report the loop and carry on (D-008). The objects themselves are
well formed; the loop is a property of the walk.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-loop/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-loop/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-loop/rsync)

#### `m3-walk-nested`: A CA publication point nested inside the TA's

ca1's caRepository is a subdirectory of the TA's publication point
(rpki/ta/ca1). The fetch of the TA's module (D-012) already brings it, so
the walk must read it from that copy and make no rsync run of its own.
This is the common shape of RIR repositories, where one fetch covers
most of the tree.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [6481 §2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-nested/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-nested/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-nested/rsync)

#### `m3-walk-shared-module`: Two sibling CAs publishing in the same rsync module

The TA certifies ca1, which certifies ca2 and ca3, each with a ROA. All of them publish under the TA's module (rpki), so the walk fetches the module once (D-012) and finds ca2's and ca3's publication points at the same level, covered by that fetch. A level's points are validated in parallel before they are reported (#169); this is the shape where a refetch of the module caused by one sibling must be seen by the other (RFC 6481 section 5, #137).

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-shared-module/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-shared-module/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-shared-module/rsync)

#### `m3-walk-siblings`: Eight CAs, each publishing in its own rsync module on one host

The TA certifies eight CAs, each publishing in a module of its own on the
TA's host (s1 to s8), so each needs its own rsync run even though whole
modules are fetched (D-012). This is the shape where per-host parallelism
still matters: many separately fetched units on one server, as
registro.br's thousands of member CAs were under D-009 (#85). The walk
fetches them concurrently, at most a fixed number at once per host
(D-011).

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-siblings/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-siblings/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-siblings/rsync)

#### `m3-walk-silent-branch`: A silent host on one branch, a deep branch elsewhere

The TA certifies ca1 and ca2. ca1 publishes on silent.example, which tests point at a server that accepts TCP connections and never answers, as some delegated repositories do (#88): each fetch from it waits for rsync's connect timeout (D-008). ca2, ca3 and ca4 form a chain, each publishing in a module of its own, so every level of that branch needs an rsync run. A walk that waits for a whole level before going on holds the deep branch up for the silent host's timeout; the walk must instead go down the deep branch while the silent fetch is still waiting (#88).

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-silent-branch/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-silent-branch/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-silent-branch/rsync)

#### `m3-walk-unreachable`: A child CA whose publication point is on an unreachable host

The TA certifies two CAs. ca1's caRepository is on unreachable.invalid,
a name that can never resolve (RFC 6761 reserves .invalid); ca2 is
normal. The walk must report the failed fetch, keep any last good copy
of ca1's publication point (RFC 8897 §7), and still mirror ca2. ca1's
files are generated under rsync/unreachable/ so a test can first serve
them, to have a last good copy, and then take the host away.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [8897 §7](../rfc/rfc8897.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8897.html#section-7))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-unreachable/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-unreachable/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m3-walk-unreachable/rsync)

#### `m6-inherit-from-empty`: Inheriting an address family the issuer doesn't hold

ca1 holds IPv4 addresses (1.0.0.0/8) and AS numbers but no IPv6; ca2 inherits both address families. RFC 3779 section 2.2.3.5 takes inherited resources from the issuer, and ca1 has no IPv6 to take, so ca2 holds no IPv6: inheriting nothing is holding nothing (D-026). Real repositories depend on this: RFC 9286 section 5.1 requires every manifest's EE certificate to inherit its resources, so under a CA without IPv6 the manifest inherits IPv6 from nothing.

Effective resources (#153): everything validates, and ca2 holds ca1's IPv4 addresses only.

- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m6-overclaim-roa-ee/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m6-overclaim-roa-ee/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m6-overclaim-roa-ee/rsync)

### M7

#### `m7-roa-max-length-below-prefix`: ROA whose maxLength is below its prefix length

The baseline tree (m0-minimal-valid) with one change: roa1.roa gives 1.1.0.0/16 a maxLength of 12. RFC 9582 section 4.3.2.2: maxLength MUST be "an integer greater than or equal to the length of the accompanying prefix". The ROA decodes (only a maxLength above the address width fails at decoding, F-012), and section 5 makes it invalid as a whole.

ROA content validation (#171).

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ca1/roa1.roa`: 1.1.0.0/16: maxLength 12 is outside 16..32
- **RFC:** [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)), [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-max-length-below-prefix/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-max-length-below-prefix/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-max-length-below-prefix/rsync)

#### `m7-roa-max-length-superfluous`: ROA with a maxLength equal to its prefix length

The baseline tree (m0-minimal-valid) with one change: roa1.roa encodes a maxLength of 16 for 1.1.0.0/16. RFC 9582 section 4.3.2.2: "The maxLength element SHOULD NOT be encoded if the maximum length is equal to the prefix length", and CAs "SHOULD anticipate that future Relying Parties will become increasingly stringent". A SHOULD only warns (D-030, F-018): the ROA is valid, with the warning superfluous_max_length.

ROA content validation (#171).

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-max-length-superfluous/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-max-length-superfluous/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-max-length-superfluous/rsync)

#### `m7-roa-not-canonical`: ROA whose prefixes are not in canonical order

The baseline tree (m0-minimal-valid) with one change: roa1.roa lists 1.1.128.0/24 before 1.1.0.0/24. RFC 9582 section 4.3.3 says ipAddrBlocks SHOULD be in canonical form, sorted by the comparator of section 4.3.3.1. A SHOULD only warns (D-030, F-018): the ROA is valid, with the warning not_canonical_order.

ROA content validation (#171).

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [9582 §4.3.3](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.3)), [9582 §4.3.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.3.1))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-not-canonical/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-not-canonical/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-not-canonical/rsync)

#### `m7-roa-prefix-outside-ee`: ROA with a prefix outside its EE certificate's addresses

The baseline tree (m0-minimal-valid) with a second ROA, roa2.roa, as Barry writes it by default, and one change: roa1.roa also lists 1.2.0.0/16, while its EE certificate holds 1.1.0.0/16 and 101::/16. RFC 9582 section 5 requires "every IP address prefix in the ROA payload is contained within the set of IP addresses specified by the EE certificate's IP address delegation extension"; if not, "the ROA in its entirety MUST be considered invalid", so the ROA's other prefixes give no VRPs either. roa2.roa, at the same publication point, stays valid. The EE certificate itself is within ca1's resources, so this is not an overclaim (RFC 6487 section 7.2).

ROA content validation (#171).

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ca1/roa1.roa`: 1.2.0.0/16 not in the EE certificate's addresses
- **RFC:** [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-prefix-outside-ee/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-prefix-outside-ee/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-roa-prefix-outside-ee/rsync)

#### `m7-vrp-duplicate`: Two ROAs stating the same VRP

ca1 publishes roa1.roa and roa2.roa, both authorizing AS64496 to originate 1.1.0.0/16, each with its own EE certificate holding that prefix. Both are valid (RFC 9582 section 5). The VRP is one authorization, so the default output lists it once; collecting VRPs (#164) keeps one per ROA, each with its URI, so `lumina vrps --wide` can show both (D-033).

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-vrp-duplicate/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-vrp-duplicate/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m7-vrp-duplicate/rsync)

## Test TALs

Hand-written Trust Anchor Locators, valid and malformed, and what a correct TAL parser must report for each (RFC 8630 §2.2, D-002).

#### `invalid-base64-character`: An illegal character in the base64 key

The key is base64 (RFC 4648 section 4); "@" is outside the alphabet.

- **Expected:** invalid: `bad_base64` at line 3
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [4648 §4](../rfc/rfc4648.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4648.html#section-4))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-base64-character/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-base64-character/case.exs)

#### `invalid-base64-padding`: Base64 key with a character missing at the end

The last character of the key is removed, so the base64 length is no
longer a multiple of four and the padding is wrong. Length and padding
errors aren't tied to one key line, so they are reported at the first
key line.

- **Expected:** invalid: `bad_base64` at line 3
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [4648 §4](../rfc/rfc4648.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4648.html#section-4))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-base64-padding/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-base64-padding/case.exs)

#### `invalid-blank-line-after-key`: A blank line after the key

After the key the file ends; a further empty line is outside the
grammar. By D-002 it is an error, not something to skip silently.

- **Expected:** invalid: `extra_blank_line` at line 4
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-blank-line-after-key/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-blank-line-after-key/case.exs)

#### `invalid-comment-after-uris`: A comment after the last URI

Same rule as a comment between URIs, at the end of the URI section.

- **Expected:** invalid: `comment_after_uris` at line 2
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-comment-after-uris/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-comment-after-uris/case.exs)

#### `invalid-comment-between-uris`: A comment between the URIs

Comments are only allowed in the comment section, before the URIs. By
D-002 a comment among the URIs is an error.

- **Expected:** invalid: `comment_after_uris` at line 2
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-comment-between-uris/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-comment-between-uris/case.exs)

#### `invalid-comment-control-character`: A control character in a comment

Comment text must conform to RFC 5198 section 2, which excludes
control characters such as BEL (0x07). RFC 5198 isn't in the library,
so this follows RFC 8630's reference to it.

- **Expected:** invalid: `invalid_comment_text` at line 1
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-comment-control-character/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-comment-control-character/case.exs)

#### `invalid-empty`: Empty file

A TAL must contain at least one URI and a key. An empty file must be
rejected, not treated as an empty TAL.

- **Expected:** invalid: `empty` at line 1
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-empty/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-empty/case.exs)

#### `invalid-empty-key`: URIs and the blank line, but no key

The key section is required. The problem is found at the end of the
file, line 3.

- **Expected:** invalid: `empty_key` at line 3
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-empty-key/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-empty-key/case.exs)

#### `invalid-ftp-uri`: An FTP URI

Any scheme other than rsync or HTTPS is unsupported.

- **Expected:** invalid: `unsupported_scheme` at line 1
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-ftp-uri/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-ftp-uri/case.exs)

#### `invalid-http-uri`: A plain HTTP URI

A TA URI MUST be rsync or HTTPS. Plain HTTP offers no integrity, so it
must be rejected even though it looks almost right.

- **Expected:** invalid: `unsupported_scheme` at line 1
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4))

#### `invalid-key-not-der`: A key that decodes but isn't DER

Valid base64 of a BER encoding with an indefinite length: it isn't
DER, which the subjectPublicKeyInfo must be.

- **Expected:** invalid: `not_der` at line 3
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))

#### `invalid-key-not-spki`: A key that is DER but not a SubjectPublicKeyInfo

Valid base64 of a valid DER INTEGER: well formed, but not a
subjectPublicKeyInfo.

- **Expected:** invalid: `not_spki` at line 3
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [5280 §4.1.2.7](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.7))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-key-not-spki/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-key-not-spki/case.exs)

#### `invalid-malformed-uri`: A URI containing a space

A URI must have valid RFC 3986 syntax; an unencoded space makes it
invalid.

- **Expected:** invalid: `invalid_uri` at line 1
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [3986 §3](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-malformed-uri/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-malformed-uri/case.exs)

#### `invalid-missing-separator`: No blank line between the URIs and the key

Without the separating line break, the first key line sits in the URI
section. A parser must recognize it as the key and report the missing
separator, rather than an odd URI.

- **Expected:** invalid: `missing_separator` at line 2
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))
- **Files:** [TAL](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-missing-separator/case.tal) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/tals/cases/invalid-missing-separator/case.exs)

#### `invalid-no-uri`: Comments, then the blank line and key, but no URI

The URI section has one or more URIs. Here the first non-comment line
is already the separator, so there is no URI.

- **Expected:** invalid: `no_uri` at line 2
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))

#### `invalid-only-comments`: Only comments

Comments alone are not a TAL: the URI section requires at least one

- **Expected:** invalid: `no_uri` at line 3
- **RFC:** [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2))

#### `invalid-relative-uri`: A relative reference instead of a URI

A TA URI must be absolute, with a scheme; a path on its own isn't a TA

- **Expected:** invalid: `invalid_uri` at line 1

Copied verbatim from the RFC, the example keeps the document's nine-

The grammar has exactly one line break between the URIs and the key.

### `Lumina.ASN1Test`

[test/lumina/asn1_test.exs](../../test/lumina/asn1_test.exs)

Tests the wrapper around the ASN.1 modules compiled from the RFCs. Every
RPKI object is decoded through it, so it must decode real objects
faithfully, reject trailing data that asn1ct would silently ignore, and
never raise on malformed input, which a validator receives from
untrusted repositories.

- *real objects:* decodes the TA certificate and re-encodes it to identical bytes (RFC [5280 §4.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1)), [5280 §A.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt))
- *real objects:* decodes and re-encodes a CRL (RFC [5280 §5.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1)), [5280 §A.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt))
- *real objects:* decodes the ROA and manifest contents through the CMS envelope (RFC [5652 §12.1](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-12.1)), [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt))
  A smoke test across modules; CMS, ROA and manifest decoding proper are #29-#31.
- *malformed input:* rejects trailing bytes after a valid value
  asn1ct decodes the value and silently drops anything after it. A
  validator must not accept an object with appended data, so the
  wrapper compiles with :undec_rest and rejects any leftover.
- *malformed input:* rejects empty, truncated and garbage input with an error, not an exception
- *malformed input:* never raises on random bytes
  Seeded, so the 2000 inputs are the same on every run.
- *malformed input:* a ROA with an address family other than IPv4 or IPv6 is an error, not a crash (RFC [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9582 §4.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.1)))
  RFC 9582's module limits addressFamily to IPv4 and IPv6 with an
  information object set, so the generated decoder exits on any other
  AFI (F-012 in doc/rfc-findings.md). The wrapper must turn that exit
  into an error.
- *malformed input:* reports an unknown module, an unknown type and non-binary input
- *malformed input:* encoding an invalid value returns an error
- every module key names a loaded, compiled ASN.1 module

### `Lumina.CacheTest`

[test/lumina/cache_test.exs](../../test/lumina/cache_test.exs)

Tests the local cache (`Lumina.Cache`, #71): the layout, staging and
swapping a fetch into place, and that a failed fetch or a crash never
loses the last good copy (RFC 8897 §7). Repository content is untrusted,
so the tests also check that symlinks and special files never reach the
cache. The content used is a real Barry fixture tree, compared byte for
byte. Crashes are simulated by leaving the cache in each state an
interrupted `commit/3` can leave it in.

- *layout and swapping:* a committed fetch is the live copy, at the module's cache path (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
- *layout and swapping:* a second commit replaces the first completely
  Files deleted upstream must disappear from the cache, not linger from the old copy.
- *layout and swapping:* a failed fetch is discarded and the last good copy stays byte-identical (RFC [8897 §7](../rfc/rfc8897.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8897.html#section-7)))
- *layout and swapping:* a commit that fails halfway puts the live copy back (RFC [8897 §7](../rfc/rfc8897.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8897.html#section-7)))
  The live copy is moved aside, then the staging directory can't be
  renamed into place (its parent is read-only): the live copy must go
  back where it was.
- *layout and swapping:* committing a staging directory that doesn't exist changes nothing
- *layout and swapping:* working directories start with a dot and never collide with repository content
- *untrusted content:* symlinks are removed and reported, and their targets aren't touched
  A repository could plant a symlink to a file outside the cache. It's
  removed before the swap, never followed, and its target is untouched.
- *untrusted content:* FIFOs and other special files are removed and reported
- *recovery after a crash:* a live copy left aside is put back (RFC [8897 §7](../rfc/rfc8897.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8897.html#section-7)))
- *recovery after a crash:* after a crash that completed the swap, only the old copy is removed
- *recovery after a crash:* leftover staging directories are removed
- *recovery after a crash:* recovering a fresh or clean cache does nothing
- *single files:* a TA certificate fetched over HTTPS is written at its cache path, replacing the old one (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
- *fetch status (D-007):* a URI never fetched has no status
- *fetch status (D-007):* a success records the attempt and the success
- *fetch status (D-007):* a failure after a success keeps the time of the last success
  The time of the last success is what tells a reader how stale the copy is.
- *fetch status (D-007):* a failure with no earlier success has no last success
- *fetch status (D-007):* statuses of different URIs are kept apart

### `Lumina.CertificateTest`

[test/lumina/certificate_test.exs](../../test/lumina/certificate_test.exs)

Tests decoding of RPKI resource certificates (RFC 5280 profiled by RFC
6487). Every later check (chain building, signatures, resources, URIs)
reads these structs, so decoding must expose every field faithfully, keep
the exact signed bytes, and stay structural: profile violations decode,
and only non-DER or unparseable input fails.

- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* the TA certificate is a self-issued v3 CA certificate valid 2026-2036 (RFC [6487 §4.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.1)), [6487 §4.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.4)), [6487 §4.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.5)), [6487 §4.6](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.6)), [6487 §4.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.1)), [6487 §4.8.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.4)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* the Subject Key Identifier is the SHA-1 of the public key bits (RFC [6487 §4.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.2)), [5280 §4.2.1.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.2.1.2)))
  The key identifier is the SHA-1 of the subjectPublicKey bit string's value.
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* the CA certificate points to the TA: AKI equals the TA's SKI and the issuer is the TA's subject (RFC [6487 §4.8.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.3)), [6487 §4.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.4)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* the CA certificate's CRL, issuer, repository and manifest URIs and policy (RFC [6487 §4.8.6](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.6)), [6487 §4.8.7](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.7)), [6487 §4.8.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.1)), [6487 §4.8.9](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.9)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* resources are decoded through Lumina.Resources (RFC [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)), [6487 §4.8.11](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.11)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* the ROA's EE certificate (RFC [6487 §4.8.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.4)), [6487 §4.8.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.2)), [6488 §2.1.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.4)))
  An EE certificate has no Basic Constraints, signs objects, and its SIA points to the signed object.
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* tbs_der is the exact tbsCertificate bytes from the input (RFC [5280 §4.1.1.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.1.1)))
  Signatures are over the exact DER of tbsCertificate, so it must be the input's bytes.
- *profile violations still decode (fixtures):* a version 2 certificate decodes with version 2 (RFC [6487 §4.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.1)))
- *profile violations still decode (fixtures):* a certificate without a Subject Key Identifier decodes without one (RFC [6487 §4.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.2)))
- *profile violations still decode (fixtures):* an unrecognized critical extension is kept, with its OID and criticality (RFC [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)))
- *malformed content:* a known extension whose value doesn't decode is marked malformed
  A broken known extension is reported in place, so validation can name it, not the whole certificate.
- *malformed content:* a validity time that isn't a real date is an error (RFC [5280 §4.1.2.5.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.5.1)))
- *malformed content:* non-DER, truncated and non-certificate input are errors naming the layer (RFC [6487 §4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4)), [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)))

### `Lumina.ChainTest`

[test/lumina/chain_test.exs](../../test/lumina/chain_test.exs)

Tests chain validation (`Lumina.Chain`, #112): RFC 6487 §7.2 points 1
to 5 and 7 (point 5 as RFC 9829 §3.2 updates it), for a TA against its
TAL and for each certificate against its issuer and the issuer's CRL.

A small top-down walk over a fixture's files (`validate/1`) stands in
for the repository walk (#113): it validates the TA, then each
certificate in the publication point of each valid CA, with the CRL its
CRLDP names. Every positive Barry fixture must validate to its leaves,
and each `m4-chain-*` fixture fails at one certificate with its rule;
certificates under an invalid CA are not validated at all.

Fixtures validate at 2030-01-01.

- *fixtures:* every positive Barry fixture validates down to its leaves (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)), [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
  Every certificate reached (TA, CAs, EE certificates of manifests
  and ROAs) is valid. Warnings are allowed: m4-cert-unknown-extension
  (D-013) and m4-crl-stale (D-016).
- *fixtures:* m4-chain-ta-bad-signature: a TA whose self-signature fails is invalid, and nothing below is validated (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
- *fixtures:* m4-chain-ta-expired: an expired TA is invalid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
- *fixtures:* m4-chain-ca-bad-signature: a CA whose signature fails with the TA's key is invalid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  Its own publication point (ca1/) is not validated.
- *fixtures:* m4-chain-issuer-mismatch: a CA whose issuer isn't the TA's subject is invalid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [5280 §6.1.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-6.1.3)))
- *fixtures:* m4-chain-aki-mismatch: a CA whose AKI isn't the TA's key identifier is invalid (RFC [6487 §4.8.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.3)))
- *fixtures:* m4-chain-crl-missing: a CA whose CRLDP names a missing CRL is invalid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)))
- *fixtures:* m4-chain-revoked-ca: a revoked CA is invalid and its sibling stays valid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)))
  D-021: Barry writes and signs the revoked entry; nothing is re-signed.
- *CRL results:* an invalid CRL makes its children invalid, naming the CRL's rules (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
- *CRL results:* a stale CRL's warning is passed on to its children (RFC [5280 §5.1.2.5](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.5)))
  D-016: the child is valid and keeps the stale_crl warning.
- *CRL results:* crl_uri/1 gives the rsync URI of the CRLDP, and nil for a TA (RFC [6487 §4.8.6](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.6)))

### `Lumina.CLISyncTest`

[test/lumina/cli_sync_test.exs](../../test/lumina/cli_sync_test.exs)

Tests `lumina sync` (#76) through `Lumina.CLI.run/4`, against real rsync
daemons serving Barry fixtures: the summary, `--tal` picking TALs,
exit codes (0 everything fetched, 1 a fetch failed, 2 usage error), the
cache lock and `lumina help sync`, and how invalid TAs and CAs are
reported (#113). Output goes to StringIO devices.

The fixture TALs name `https://localhost:8443` and
`rsync://localhost:8873`. Each test writes a copy of the TAL whose rsync
URI points at its own daemon, and remaps `localhost:8873` in the
repository's certificates to it (`:remap`, see `Lumina.Walk`).

- *syncing:* a full sync exits 0 and prints the TA URI, publication points and fetches (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
- *syncing:* an invalid CA is listed with its reasons, and isn't walked (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  D-014: an invalid CA isn't a fetch failure; the sync exits 0.
- *syncing:* a publication point that fails is counted and listed with its reasons (RFC [9286 §6.5](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.5)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
  Like an invalid CA, a failed publication point isn't a fetch failure: exit 0.
- *syncing:* a point that fails after a good sync is counted as served from its last valid copy (RFC [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
  D-023: served from a copy whose ROA changes between two syncs.
- *syncing:* a TA that doesn't validate is rejected with its reasons, exit 1 (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
- *syncing:* --tal syncs only the TAL it names
  Requested by the maintainer: --tal syncs that TAL only. The tals
  folder also holds a TAL that can't be reached; it must not be tried.
- *syncing:* without --tal, every TAL in the TAL folder is synced
- *syncing:* a failure below the trust anchor's publication point exits 0 with a warning, named (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  m3-walk-unreachable: the delegated CA's host doesn't resolve. The
  trust anchor and its own publication point synced, so the exit code
  is 0 (D-037, #187), with the failure listed and a warning.
- *syncing:* a trust anchor whose own publication point can't be fetched exits 1
  The TA is retrieved from the daemon, but the repository host in its
  certificate points at a closed port: its own publication point is
  never fetched (#187).
- *syncing:* a TAL whose TA can't be fetched exits 1, with each attempt listed (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
- *sync times (#185):* each TAL whose tree was walked gets its sync time recorded
  lumina vrps --sync measures a TAL's age from this record. A TAL
  whose TA can't be retrieved, with none stored, gets none.
- *overclaims (#155):* an overclaiming CA certificate is listed with the resources outside its issuer's, and counted (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
  m6-overclaim-ipv4: ca2 claims 2.0.0.0/16, outside ca1's. Like any
  invalid CA it isn't a fetch failure (exit 0), and it isn't
  walked.
- *overclaims (#155):* a signed object's overclaim is not reported by sync (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
  The walk validates CA certificates only, so a ROA whose EE
  certificate overclaims (m6-overclaim-roa-ee) is lumina
  validate's to report.
- *overclaims (#155):* a sync without overclaims prints no overclaims line
- *--per-host (#98):* --per-host 1 makes at most one rsync run at a time per host
  m3-walk-siblings (eight sibling publication points) from a daemon
  that refuses a second connection: with --per-host 1 every fetch
  gets through, so the flag reaches the walk.
- *--per-host (#98):* --per-host above what the server accepts gets fetches refused
  The converse: with --per-host 8 the same daemon refuses some fetches.
- *--per-host (#98):* --per-host must be a number of at least 1
- *the cache lock:* a cache held by a running process isn't touched, and the sync exits 1
- *the cache lock:* a lock whose process is gone is taken over
  A lock left by a crashed run (its process is gone) is taken over and released.
- *rsync (#89, #93):* an rsync older than 3.1.0 stops the sync before anything is fetched, exit 1
  The cache isn't created: nothing is fetched and no lock is taken.
- *rsync (#89, #93):* openrsync is recognised as too old
  macOS's /usr/bin/rsync is openrsync, which reports itself as 2.6.9 compatible.
- *rsync (#89, #93):* --rsync naming a missing file stops the sync, naming the path, exit 1
- *rsync (#89, #93):* --rsync naming a file that isn't executable stops the sync, exit 1
- *rsync (#89, #93):* --rsync is the binary used for every rsync run (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  The binary given is a wrapper that logs each call and runs the real
  rsync. The sync must succeed, and every rsync run (version check,
  TA retrieval and walk) must have gone through the wrapper.
- *rsync (#89, #93):* an rsync that rejects its arguments is reported with rsync's message
  An rsync that passes the version check but rejects an argument
  (exit 1): the fetch fails as usage_error, and rsync's own message
  is in the summary.
- *usage:* --tal on a missing file is a usage error
- *usage:* --tal on a file that isn't a TAL is a usage error (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
- *usage:* an unknown flag, a stray argument or a bad number is a usage error
- *usage:* an empty TAL folder without --tal is a usage error
- *usage:* lumina help sync describes the flags and exit codes
- *usage:* lumina help lists sync

### `Lumina.CLITest`

[test/lumina/cli_test.exs](../../test/lumina/cli_test.exs)

Tests the `lumina` command line through `Lumina.CLI.run/3`, which returns
the exit code instead of halting. The CLI follows the command plus flags
model (D-001 in doc/decisions.md): `lumina print [--brief] FILE...`,
`lumina help [command]`. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 a file failed to
decode, 2 usage error. Output goes to StringIO devices.

- *print:* prints one file in full and exits 0
- *print:* --brief leaves out cryptographic detail and keeps the payload
- *print:* --brief may come after the files
- *print:* several files print one section each, with a header
- *print:* a file that doesn't decode is reported on stderr, and the exit code is 1
- *print:* an unknown file type and a missing file are decode failures
- *print:* print with no files, or an unknown flag, prints the print usage and exits 2
- *print:* a TAL prints, and a malformed TAL exits 1 with the line number (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
- *print:* print --help shows the print usage
- *help and usage:* help, -h and --help print the general usage and exit 0
- *help and usage:* help <command> prints that command's usage
- *help and usage:* no arguments, an unknown command, or the old --print flag exit 2 with usage
  The first version used a --print flag (PR #53); under D-001 it's a usage error.

### `Lumina.CLIValidateTest`

[test/lumina/cli_validate_test.exs](../../test/lumina/cli_validate_test.exs)

Tests offline validation of the cache (#114, D-014): `Lumina.Validate.run/3`
and `lumina validate` through `Lumina.CLI.run/4`.

Each test first fills a cache with a sync of a Barry fixture from a
local rsync daemon (as `Lumina.CLISyncTest` does), then validates that
cache without fetching. Validation must give the same verdicts on CA
certificates as the walk gave during the sync, and adds the EE
signed objects (CMS envelope and EE certificate, #131).

Syncs run at 2026-11-13, inside the fixtures' default validity.

- *verdicts:* validating a synced cache gives the walk's verdicts on every Barry fixture (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  Every fixture whose TA a sync accepts. The CA certificates found
  invalid offline are exactly those the walk reported invalid, and a
  positive fixture has nothing invalid at all, signed objects
  included.
- *verdicts:* an invalid CA is listed with its reasons, nothing below it is validated, exit 1 (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)))
  One of four certificates invalid is more than the default 10% (D-022).
- *verdicts:* --max-invalid sets the share of invalid certificates a run may have and still exit 0
  m4-chain-revoked-ca has one invalid certificate of four (25%):
  --max-invalid 0 and 24 fail, 25 and 100 pass (D-022).
- *verdicts:* a valid tree exits 0 and counts CA certificates and signed objects by type (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [6487 §4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4)))
  m0-minimal-valid: ca1, two manifests and a ROA.
- *signed objects (#131, #132):* a signed object whose CMS envelope or manifest content is invalid is listed with its rule (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [9589 §4](../rfc/rfc9589.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9589.html#section-4)), [9286 §4.4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.4)))
  Driven by the metadata of every m5-cms-* and m5-mft-* fixture: the
  object it names is listed invalid with its (first) rule, and nothing
  else is.
- *--now:* --now after the fixture's expiry finds the TA expired, and nothing below valid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  After the fixtures' notAfter (2036-01-01), the TA itself has expired.
- *--now:* --now sets the validation time for every certificate (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  m4-cert-expired's ca1 expires before 2030; the sync, in 2026, followed it.
- *publication points (#134):* a point that fails is its manifest's invalid entry, and nothing in it is validated (RFC [9286 §6.3](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.3)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
  m5-pp-manifest-stale's ca1.mft goes stale on 2027-01-01. The sync
  (2026-11-13) accepted the point; validating at 2030 fails it, and
  its ROA isn't validated.
- *publication points (#134):* files not on a manifest are counted and not validated (RFC [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)))
  Files not on the manifest "MUST NOT be used": counted, never validated.
- *last valid copy (D-023, #135):* a point that fails offline is validated from its last valid copy (RFC [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
  The sync kept each accepted point. A listed file then changes in
  the mirror: validate falls back to the kept copy, says so, and the
  ROA is still validated.
- *overclaims (#155):* an overclaiming CA certificate is listed with the resources outside its issuer's, and counted (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
  m6-overclaim-ipv4: ca2 claims 2.0.0.0/16, outside ca1's
  1.0.0.0/8. The line names the prefix after the rule, and the TAL
  summary counts one overclaim.
- *overclaims (#155):* a signed object whose EE certificate overclaims is listed with the resources, and counted (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
  m6-overclaim-roa-ee: the EE certificate of roa1.roa claims 2.0.0.0/16.
- *overclaims (#155):* an AS range partly outside the issuer's is listed as the part outside (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
  m6-overclaim-as-range: only the half of ca2's AS range above ca1's is named.
- *overclaims (#155):* an overclaim counts as invalid toward --max-invalid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  m6-overclaim-grandchild: one invalid object (ca3) of nine, 11%:
  above the default 10%, within --max-invalid 12 (D-022).
- *overclaims (#155):* a tree without overclaims prints no overclaims line
- *failures and usage:* a cache without the TAL's TA exits 1 and says to sync first
- *failures and usage:* a valid CA whose publication point isn't in the cache is reported missing, exit 0 (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  Missing publication points are a fetch problem, reported by sync (D-022).
- *failures and usage:* a bad --now or --max-invalid, an unknown flag or a stray argument is a usage error
- *failures and usage:* lumina help validate describes the flags and exit codes

### `Lumina.CLIVRPsTest`

[test/lumina/cli_vrps_test.exs](../../test/lumina/cli_vrps_test.exs)

Tests `lumina vrps` (#165, D-031): it validates the cache offline, as
`lumina validate` does, and writes the VRPs of the valid ROAs as CSV in
Routinator's columns (D-032), one row per distinct AS, prefix,
maxLength and trust anchor (D-033), to stdout or atomically to
`--output FILE`, as CSV or as JSON (`--format json`, #167, RFC 8259,
`doc/output.md`). Above `--max-invalid` the VRPs are still written, with
a warning, and the exit code is 1 (D-034).

Each test syncs Barry fixtures from a local rsync daemon with `lumina
sync`, then runs `lumina vrps` at 2030-01-01 (`--now`), through
`Lumina.CLI.run/4`.

- *CSV output:* a fixture's VRPs are written as CSV, header first, in order (RFC [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)), [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
  m1-roa-prefixes: AS64496 with 1.1.0.0/17-24, 1.1.128.0/24 and 0101::/16-48.
- *CSV output:* with two TALs, each VRP carries its own trust anchor's name
  m0-minimal-valid's TAL under two names: each VRP once per trust
  anchor, named after its TAL file (D-032), in the VRP order.
- *CSV output:* a VRP stated by two ROAs is written once
  m7-vrp-duplicate: roa1.roa and roa2.roa both state AS64496, 1.1.0.0/16 (D-033).
- *--wide (#166):* adds the ROA's URI and lists a VRP once per ROA that states it
  m7-vrp-duplicate: roa1.roa and roa2.roa both state AS64496,
  1.1.0.0/16. --wide lists it once for each, with its ROA's URI
  (D-033); without it, once.
- *--wide (#166):* every row's URI is the ROA the VRP comes from, in the default order
  m1-roa-prefixes: one ROA, so each row's URI is roa1.roa.
- *--format json (#167):* a fixture's JSON decodes to exactly the expected document (RFC [8259 §4](../rfc/rfc8259.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html#section-4)), [8259 §5](../rfc/rfc8259.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html#section-5)), [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
  m1-roa-prefixes: the whole document, metadata and the three VRPs,
  as `:json.decode/1` gives it.
- *--format json (#167):* the JSON has the same VRPs as the CSV, in the same order
  m0-minimal-valid's TAL under two names: the JSON rows, written as
  CSV rows, are the CSV's rows, in its order, and each trust anchor
  counts its own.
- *--format json (#167):* with --wide, each VRP has its ROA's URI and duplicates are kept
  m7-vrp-duplicate: with --wide, each row has "uri" and the VRP that
  roa1.roa and roa2.roa both state is there twice (D-033).
- *--format json (#167):* quotes, backslashes and control characters in a name are escaped (RFC [8259 §7](../rfc/rfc8259.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html#section-7)))
  A TAL file named with a double quote, a backslash and a control
  character (U+0001): JSON escapes them in the trust anchor's name,
  and decoding gives the name back. The solidus in a prefix stays
  unescaped, as §7's prose allows (F-036).
- *--format json (#167):* each trust anchor's status says why the run failed
  m7-roa-prefix-outside-ee (over --max-invalid, D-034) and a TAL with
  no trust anchor in the cache: each one's status, and the VRPs
  still written for the first.
- *--format json (#167):* with no VRPs, roas is an empty array
- *--sync (#185):* with an empty cache, the TAL is synced and its VRPs written
- *--sync (#185):* a TAL synced within --max-age isn't synced again
  Synced 10 minutes before, within the default --max-age of 1h: no
  sync, shown by the repository host now pointing at a closed port,
  which would fail one.
- *--sync (#185):* a TAL last synced longer ago than --max-age is synced
- *--sync (#185):* only the TALs that need it are synced, and a failed sync still writes the VRPs
  Two TALs: case.tal, synced a minute ago, and dead.tal, with
  m0-minimal-valid's key (so its own trust anchor) and only a URI
  at a closed port. Only dead.tal is synced; that sync fails, and
  case.tal's VRPs are still written, with exit 1.
- *--sync (#185):* a fetch failing below the trust anchor's own publication point only warns
  m3-walk-unreachable: the TA's publication point is fetched, the
  delegated CA's host (unreachable.invalid) isn't. The sync's
  failure is reported, but the trust anchor synced, so the exit
  code is 0 (D-037).
- *--sync (#185):* a TAL counts as synced only if its TA and the TA's own publication point were fetched
  Reports as Lumina.Sync.run/3 gives them, reduced to what matters.
- *--sync (#185):* sync flags without --sync, and a bad --max-age, are usage errors
- *--output:* writes the same bytes as standard output, and nothing to standard output
- *--output:* a file that can't be written fails with exit 1 and leaves nothing behind
- *failures:* above --max-invalid the VRPs are still written, with a warning, and exit 1 (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
  m7-roa-prefix-outside-ee: one invalid ROA of five objects, 20%,
  above the default 10% (D-022). roa2.roa's VRPs are written anyway
  (D-034).
- *failures:* a TAL with no trust anchor in the cache gives no rows, and exit 1
- *Lumina.VRP.csv/2:* a field holding a comma or a quote is quoted, its quotes doubled
  Lumina.URI accepts a comma in a path; the field is quoted so the columns hold.
- *usage:* an unknown format is a usage error
- *usage:* lumina help vrps describes the command and its flags

### `Lumina.CMSTest`

[test/lumina/cms_test.exs](../../test/lumina/cms_test.exs)

Tests the CMS envelope of signed objects: `Lumina.CMS.profile/1`
(#129) against RFC 6488 §2.1 and §3 item 1, as updated by RFC 9589 §4,
with the algorithms of RFC 7935 §2; and `Lumina.CMS.verify/1` (#130),
the message digest (RFC 5652 §5.4) and signature (RFC 6488 §3 item 2).

Every signed object of the positive fixtures must pass and verify, and
each `m5-cms-*` fixture must fail with exactly its one rule. Barry (pinned
`478ee89`) can't write signed attributes other than its own, unsigned
attributes, CRLs or SignedData digest algorithms (doc/barry.md), so
those rules are tested on a decoded m0-minimal-valid ROA changed in
memory: the profile checks the decoded structure, so nothing needs
re-encoding.

- *fixtures:* every signed object of the positive Barry fixtures follows the CMS profile and verifies (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [9589 §4](../rfc/rfc9589.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9589.html#section-4)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)), [5652 §5.4](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-5.4)))
  Manifests and ROAs; Barry writes content-type, signing-time and
  message-digest. The only problem allowed is the warning for
  rsaEncryption parameters left absent, which Barry always does
  (F-031).
- *fixtures:* m5-cms-bad-signature: a signature that doesn't verify with the EE certificate's key is rejected (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [8017 §8.2.2](../rfc/rfc8017.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017.html#section-8.2.2)))
- *fixtures:* m5-cms-version-1: a SignedData version other than 3 is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.1)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *fixtures:* m5-cms-signer-version-1: a SignerInfo version other than 3 is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.1)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *fixtures:* m5-cms-sid-issuer-serial: a signer identified by issuer and serial number is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.2)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *fixtures:* m5-cms-sid-mismatch: a sid that isn't the EE certificate's SKI is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.2)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *fixtures:* m5-cms-digest-sha1: a SignerInfo digest algorithm other than SHA-256 is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.3)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
- *fixtures:* m5-cms-signature-algorithm: sha1WithRSAEncryption as the signature algorithm is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.5](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.5)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
- *fixtures:* m5-cms-content-type-mismatch: a content-type attribute that isn't the eContentType is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.4.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4.1)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *SignedData:* two digest algorithms, or none, are rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.2)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *SignedData:* a SignedData digest algorithm other than SHA-256 is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.2)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
- *SignedData:* SHA-256 parameters may be absent or NULL, nothing else (RFC [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)), [5754 §2](../rfc/rfc5754.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5754.html#section-2)))
  RFC 5754 §2: absent and NULL parameters must both be accepted; anything else isn't.
- *SignedData:* no certificate, or two, is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.4)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *SignedData:* a crls field is rejected, even an empty one (RFC [6488 §2.1.5](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.5)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
  Decoding keeps an absent crls field as nil and an empty one as [], so both are told apart.
- *SignedData:* an absent eContent is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.3.2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.3.2)))
- *SignedData:* two SignerInfos are rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *signature algorithm parameters:* rsaEncryption parameters NULL pass, absent warn, anything else fails (RFC [3370 §3.2](../rfc/rfc3370.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3370.html#section-3.2)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
  F-031: RFC 3370 §3.2 requires NULL; Barry leaves them out, so absent only warns.
- *verification:* an eContent changed after signing fails the message digest (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [5652 §5.4](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-5.4)), [5652 §11.2](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-11.2)))
  The signature covers the signed attributes, so only the digest check sees the change.
- *verification:* signed attributes changed after signing fail the signature (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [5652 §5.4](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-5.4)))
- *verification:* the signature verifies with sha256WithRSAEncryption named instead of rsaEncryption (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
  RFC 7935 §2: RPs accept either; Barry signs with rsaEncryption.
- *verification:* verification skips what the profile already reports missing
  Those are profile/1's problems; verify/1 doesn't report them twice.
- *SignerInfo:* sha256WithRSAEncryption is accepted as the signature algorithm (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.5](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.5)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
  RFC 7935 §2: RPs accept either; Barry writes rsaEncryption.
- *SignerInfo:* unsigned attributes are rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.7](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.7)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *signed attributes:* absent signed attributes are rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *signed attributes:* a missing signing-time attribute is rejected (RFC [9589 §4](../rfc/rfc9589.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9589.html#section-4)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
  RFC 9589 §4 makes signing-time mandatory; RFC 6488 alone allowed leaving it out.
- *signed attributes:* a manifest whose content-type attribute isn't id-ct-rpkiManifest is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.3](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.3)), [6488 §2.1.6.4.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4.1)))
  The ROA OID (id-ct-routeOriginAuthz) in a manifest's content-type attribute.
- *signed attributes:* a missing content-type or message-digest attribute is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.4.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4.1)), [6488 §2.1.6.4.2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4.2)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *signed attributes:* a binary-signing-time attribute is rejected (RFC [9589 §4](../rfc/rfc9589.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9589.html#section-4)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
  RFC 9589 §4 removes binary-signing-time from the allowed attributes.
- *signed attributes:* any other attribute is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *signed attributes:* an attribute twice, or with two values, is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4)))
- *signed attributes:* an attribute value that doesn't decode is rejected (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4)))

### `Lumina.CRLTest`

[test/lumina/crl_test.exs](../../test/lumina/crl_test.exs)

Tests decoding of CRLs (RFC 5280 §5, profiled by RFC 6487 §5). Revocation
checks and the CRL validation in M4 read these structs, so decoding must
expose issuer, dates, CRL Number and revoked entries faithfully, keep the
exact signed bytes, and stay structural: profile violations decode.

- *the m0-minimal-valid CRLs:* decode as v2 CRLs valid 2026-2036 with no revoked certificates (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)), [5280 §5.1.2.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.1)), [5280 §5.1.2.4](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.4)), [5280 §5.1.2.5](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.5)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid CRLs:* each CRL names its issuing CA and carries that CA's key identifier (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)), [5280 §5.1.2.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.3)), [5280 §5.2.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.2.1)))
  A CRL is matched to its issuer by name and by AKI = the issuer's SKI.
- *the m0-minimal-valid CRLs:* tbs_der is the exact tbsCertList bytes from the input (RFC [5280 §5.1.1.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.1.3)))
  Signatures are over the exact DER of tbsCertList, so it must be the input's bytes.
- *revoked certificates:* revoked entries decode with serial, date and entry extensions (RFC [5280 §5.1.2.6](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.6)), [5280 §5.3.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.3.1)))
  Barry can't write revoked entries yet (revokedCertificates is on its
  README's list of unimplemented fields), so this CRL is Barry's,
  decoded, given two entries and re-encoded.
- *structural decoding:* a CRL without a version field is version 1 (RFC [5280 §5.1.2.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.1)))
- *structural decoding:* a CRL without nextUpdate decodes with next_update nil (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)), [5280 §5.1.2.5](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.5)))
  nextUpdate is OPTIONAL in the ASN.1; requiring it is the profile's job (M4).
- *structural decoding:* a CRL Number that doesn't decode is marked malformed, and number/1 is nil (RFC [5280 §5.2.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.2.3)), [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)))
- *structural decoding:* non-DER, truncated and non-CRL input are errors naming the layer

### `Lumina.CryptoTest`

[test/lumina/crypto_test.exs](../../test/lumina/crypto_test.exs)

Tests signature verification of certificates and CRLs (`Lumina.Crypto`,
#108): RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256 (RFC 7935 §2, RFC 8017 §8.2) over
2048-bit RSA keys with exponent 65,537 (RFC 7935 §3).

Barry signs every fixture correctly, so all its signatures must verify;
each rejection is shown by changing one thing in a real signature, or by
a key generated in the test. Chain validation (#112) builds on this, so
a wrong `:ok` here would let forged objects through.
