- *valid signatures:* every certificate and CRL signature in every Barry fixture verifies with its issuer's key (RFC [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)), [8017 §8.2.2](../rfc/rfc8017.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017.html#section-8.2.2)), [5280 §4.1.1.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.1.3)), [5280 §5.1.1.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.1.3)))
  Certificates (TA, CA, and the EE certificates in manifests and
  ROAs) and CRLs, each checked with the key of the certificate whose
  subject and key identifier its issuer and AKI name; a TA with its
  own key. Fixtures that break exactly that link or the signature
  are left out; their own tests are in Lumina.ProfileCRLTest and
  Lumina.ChainTest.
- *valid signatures:* a signature made by OTP's public_key verifies (RFC [8017 §8.2](../rfc/rfc8017.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017.html#section-8.2)))
  An independent check of the implementation: OTP's `:public_key`
  signs with a fresh key, and Lumina verifies.
- *valid signatures:* sha256WithRSAEncryption with absent parameters is accepted (RFC [4055 §5](../rfc/rfc4055.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4055.html#section-5)))
- *tampering:* a flipped bit in the signature is rejected (RFC [8017 §8.2.2](../rfc/rfc8017.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017.html#section-8.2.2)))
- *tampering:* a flipped bit in the signed bytes is rejected (RFC [8017 §8.2.2](../rfc/rfc8017.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017.html#section-8.2.2)), [5280 §5.1.1.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.1.3)))
- *tampering:* a signature checked with a key other than the issuer's is rejected (RFC [8017 §8.2.2](../rfc/rfc8017.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017.html#section-8.2.2)))
  The TA's signature over ca1, checked with ca1's own key.
- *tampering:* a signature not below the modulus is rejected before exponentiation (RFC [8017 §5.2.2](../rfc/rfc8017.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017.html#section-5.2.2)))
- *tampering:* a signature one octet short is rejected (RFC [8017 §8.2.2](../rfc/rfc8017.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017.html#section-8.2.2)))
  Step 1: the signature must be as long as the modulus.
- *tampering:* a signature BIT STRING that isn't whole octets is rejected (RFC [5280 §4.1.1.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.1.3)))
- *algorithms:* sha1WithRSAEncryption is rejected as unsupported (RFC [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
- *algorithms:* sha384WithRSAEncryption is rejected as unsupported (RFC [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
  A stronger hash is still not the RPKI suite: only SHA-256 is allowed.
- *algorithms:* sha256WithRSAEncryption with parameters other than NULL is rejected (RFC [4055 §5](../rfc/rfc4055.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4055.html#section-5)))
- *keys:* a 1024-bit key is rejected with the key-size reason (RFC [7935 §3](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-3)))
  The signature is otherwise valid; only the key size is wrong.
- *keys:* a 4096-bit key is rejected with the key-size reason (RFC [7935 §3](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-3)))
- *keys:* a 2048-bit key with exponent 3 is rejected with the exponent reason (RFC [7935 §3](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-3)))
- *keys:* a key whose algorithm is sha256WithRSAEncryption is read like rsaEncryption (RFC [7935 §3.1](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-3.1)), [4055 §1.2](../rfc/rfc4055.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4055.html#section-1.2)))
  F-027: RFC 7935 §3.1 names sha256WithRSAEncryption as the
  subjectPublicKeyInfo algorithm, RFC 4055 §1.2 rsaEncryption; both
  read the same RSAPublicKey.
- *keys:* a key that isn't RSA is rejected as unsupported (RFC [7935 §3.1](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-3.1)))
- *keys:* an rsaEncryption key without NULL parameters is rejected (RFC [4055 §1.2](../rfc/rfc4055.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4055.html#section-1.2)))
- *keys:* a key that isn't a DER RSAPublicKey is rejected as malformed (RFC [4055 §1.2](../rfc/rfc4055.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4055.html#section-1.2)))
- *keys:* an RSAPublicKey with a negative modulus is rejected as malformed (RFC [4055 §1.2](../rfc/rfc4055.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4055.html#section-1.2)))

### `Lumina.DERTest`

[test/lumina/der_test.exs](../../test/lumina/der_test.exs)

Tests strict DER checking. RPKI requires DER (RFC 6488 §3 (l), RFC 6481
§2.2), but OTP's decoders accept BER, so every DER rule is checked here:
for each one, a minimal hand-built violation must be rejected with the
right rule and X.690 clause, and its valid counterpart accepted. X.690
isn't in doc/rfc, so its clauses are cited in each test's doc tag.

- *length octets:* rejects indefinite length
  X.690 10.1: DER uses the definite form only.
- *length octets:* rejects the long form for a short length
  X.690 10.1: lengths below 128 must use the one-octet short form.
- *length octets:* rejects a long-form length with a leading zero octet
  X.690 10.1: minimum number of octets, so no leading zero length octet.
- *length octets:* rejects the reserved length octet
  X.690 8.1.3.5: the first length octet 0xFF is reserved.
- *length octets:* rejects truncated input at every layer
- *identifier octets:* rejects the high-tag-number form for a low tag number
  X.690 8.1.2.2: tag numbers 0-30 use the single-octet form.
- *identifier octets:* rejects a high tag number with a leading 0x80 octet
  X.690 8.1.2.4.2: the first subsequent tag octet must not be 0x80.
- *identifier octets:* rejects end-of-contents octets
  X.690 8.1.5: end-of-contents octets only close indefinite lengths, which DER forbids.
- *primitive and constructed forms:* rejects a constructed OCTET STRING
  X.690 10.2: BIT STRING, OCTET STRING and character strings must be primitive.
- *primitive and constructed forms:* rejects a primitive SEQUENCE
  X.690 8.9.1 and 8.11.1: SEQUENCE and SET encodings are constructed.
- *universal types:* BOOLEAN
  X.690 11.1: TRUE is 0xFF; X.690 8.2.1: exactly one contents octet.
- *universal types:* INTEGER
  X.690 8.3.1 and 8.3.2: at least one octet, minimal two's complement.
- *universal types:* BIT STRING
  X.690 8.6.2.2-8.6.2.3: unused-bits octet 0-7, and 0 when empty; X.690 11.2.1: unused bits are zero.
- *universal types:* NULL
  X.690 8.8.2: NULL has no contents.
- *universal types:* OBJECT IDENTIFIER
  X.690 8.19.2: subidentifiers are minimal (no leading 0x80) and the last one terminates.
- *universal types:* UTCTime
  X.690 11.8: UTCTime is YYMMDDHHMMSSZ, seconds present, Z, no offset.
- *universal types:* GeneralizedTime
  X.690 11.7: GeneralizedTime ends in Z with seconds; fractional seconds don't end in 0.
- *universal types:* SET OF must be sorted
  X.690 11.6: SET OF elements in ascending order of their encodings.
- *structure:* rejects trailing bytes after the encoding
  X.690 8.1.1: an encoding is one TLV. RFC 6481 §2.2 and RFC 6488 §3 don't
  say what follows it; Lumina rejects anything (F-010 in doc/rfc-findings.md).
- *structure:* checks inside constructed values of any class, and reports the inner offset
- never raises on random bytes or random mutations of a real object
  Seeded, so the inputs are the same every run. Repository content is
  untrusted, so the checker must return an error, never raise. This
  test found a crash on an empty BIT STRING.
- *fixtures:* every object in m0-minimal-valid is DER (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)))
- *fixtures:* certificates and CRLs re-encode to identical bytes (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)))
- *check_canonical/3:* rejects an encoded DEFAULT value that a TLV walk can't see (RFC [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt))
  X.690 11.5: a component equal to its DEFAULT is not encoded. A manifest
  with an explicit `version [0] INTEGER 0` passes the TLV walk, since every
  TLV is well formed, but isn't DER. Only re-encoding catches it.
- *check_canonical/3:* passes on decoding errors from the ASN.1 layer

### `Lumina.EffectiveResourcesTest`

[test/lumina/effective_resources_test.exs](../../test/lumina/effective_resources_test.exs)

Tests effective resources (#153): `Lumina.Resources.effective/2`
resolves `inherit` from the issuer's effective resources (RFC 3779
§2.2.3.5 for each address family, §3.2.3.3 for AS numbers), and
`Lumina.Chain` carries them down a chain.

Resource inclusion itself (RFC 6487 §7.2 point 6) is
`ResourceInclusionTest`'s (#154); here only
what a certificate holds is decided. Resolving gives no errors:
inheriting a kind the issuer doesn't hold is holding nothing of it
(D-026), as every manifest's EE certificate does under a CA that lacks
a kind (RFC 9286 §5.1). The unit tests change m0-minimal-valid's ca1
certificate in memory; the `m6-inherit-*` and
m1-resources-inherit fixtures check the same through real chains, at
2030-01-01.

- *Resources.effective/2:* explicit resources are taken as they are, whatever the issuer holds (RFC [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)), [6487 §4.8.11](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.11)))
- *Resources.effective/2:* an inherited kind takes the issuer's effective set, each address family on its own (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [3779 §3.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.3)))
- *Resources.effective/2:* a kind the certificate doesn't list is empty (RFC [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)), [6487 §4.8.11](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.11)))
  Only AS numbers, or one address family: the rest is held by nobody.
- *Resources.effective/2:* inheriting a kind the issuer doesn't hold is holding nothing of it (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [3779 §3.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.3)), [9286 §5.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-5.1)))
  D-026. A manifest's EE certificate must inherit every kind (RFC
  9286 §5.1), so under a CA without IPv6 or AS numbers it inherits
  them from nothing; LACNIC's repository has over 1,500 such
  manifests.
- *Resources.effective/2:* a TA's inherit resolves to nothing (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)))
  The TA's inherit is rejected against its TAL; resolving adds nothing.
- *Chain:* a child's result carries its effective resources, from the issuer's passed in (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
- *fixtures:* m6-inherit-two-levels: inheritance two levels deep resolves to ca1's resources (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [3779 §3.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.3)))
  ca2 and ca3 inherit, and so does the EE certificate of ca3's ROA.
- *fixtures:* m6-inherit-ee: an EE certificate that inherits holds its CA's addresses (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)))
- *fixtures:* m6-inherit-from-empty: inheriting IPv6 from an IPv4-only issuer holds no IPv6, and is valid (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [9286 §5.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-5.1)))
- *fixtures:* m1-resources-inherit: ca2 inherits everything from ca1 (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [3779 §3.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.3)))

### `Lumina.EncompassTest`

[test/lumina/encompass_test.exs](../../test/lumina/encompass_test.exs)

Tests the resource set operations resource inclusion needs (#152):
`Lumina.Resources.intervals/2`, `encompasses?/2` and `outside/2`.

RFC 6487 §7.1 defines "encompass" through "more specific" and "equal"
ranges; RFC 3779 §2.3 and §3.3 say a certificate's resources must be
"subsumed by" its issuer's. IPv4, IPv6 and AS numbers are compared
separately (erratum 5188 to RFC 6487 §7.1), and as sets, not range by
range (D-027, F-034): a child range spanning two adjacent ranges of a
parent is encompassed. `outside/2` gives exactly what an overclaim
claims beyond the issuer, for reporting (#155).

- *encompassed:* equal sets encompass each other (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
- *encompassed:* more specific ranges are encompassed (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
- *encompassed:* a prefix and a range covering the same addresses are equal (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.2.3.7](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.7)))
  10.0.0.0/8 written as the range 10.0.0.0-10.255.255.255, either way round.
- *encompassed:* AS ids and ranges mix: ids inside a range, and a range made of ids (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
- *encompassed:* a child range spanning two adjacent parent ranges is encompassed (set semantics) (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
  D-027, F-034. The parent lists 10.0.0.0/9 and 10.128.0.0/9, which
  RFC 3779 §2.2.3.6 says must be combined (the profile rejects
  that); the child's 10.0.0.0/8 spans both. Read literally, RFC
  6487 §7.1 wants one range of the parent to cover it.
- *encompassed:* the empty set is encompassed by anything, even the empty set (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
- *not encompassed:* one address outside, at either boundary, and the difference is exactly that address (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
  One address below 10.0.0.0/8, then one above; the difference is that address.
- *not encompassed:* one AS number outside, at either boundary, and the difference is exactly that number (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
- *not encompassed:* the difference is shown as prefixes where they fit, ranges otherwise (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
  The gap between two parent ranges is shown as prefixes where it is one, else a range.
- *not encompassed:* nothing non-empty is encompassed by the empty set (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
- *not encompassed:* IPv4, IPv6 and AS numbers are independent (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
  Erratum 5188: §7.1 compares "two IP address or two AS number sets".
  The IPv4 and IPv6 address families are separate too: 0.0.0.0/0
  doesn't cover ::/96, though both are the integers 0 to 2^32-1.
- *extremes:* the ends of the address and AS number spaces (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
  0.0.0.0/0, ::/0 and AS0-AS4294967295 hold everything; the last address or number of each is outside anything that stops one short.
- *intervals/2:* sorts, merges overlapping and adjacent entries, and drops inverted ranges (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.6](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.6)), [3779 §3.2.3.4](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.4)))
  Unsorted, overlapping and adjacent entries, as a non-canonical certificate might list them.
- *against brute force:* outside/2 matches a number-by-number set difference (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
  1,000 pairs of random AS sets within 0..63 (fixed seed), mixing
  ids and ranges, overlapping and adjacent: `outside/2` must give
  exactly the numbers of y not in x, and `encompasses?/2` must agree.

### `Lumina.Fixtures.M0MinimalValidTest`

[test/lumina/fixtures/m0_minimal_valid_test.exs](../../test/lumina/fixtures/m0_minimal_valid_test.exs)

Checks that the m0-minimal-valid fixture loads and contains the files Barry
should produce for a TA -> CA -> ROA tree. This proves the fixture
pipeline works end to end (descriptor, generation, metadata, test helper)
before any object is decoded. Decoding and validation start in M1.

- loads with its metadata
- the rsync tree contains exactly the expected objects, each non-empty and readable
- RPKI objects are DER: each file starts with a SEQUENCE tag
- the TAL's rsync URI points to the trust anchor certificate in the tree
- the TAL's public key is base64 that decodes to a DER SEQUENCE
- the RRDP files are present

### `Lumina.HTTPSTest`

[test/lumina/https_test.exs](../../test/lumina/https_test.exs)

Tests the HTTPS fetcher (`Lumina.HTTPS`, #73) against a local TLS server
(`Lumina.Test.HTTPSServer`) whose CA and certificates are made in each
test, so nothing depends on the network or on the system's CA store.

RFC 8630 §4 makes TLS certificate and host name validation mandatory for
TA certificates fetched over HTTPS, and asks for validation issues to be
logged: each kind of bad certificate must be rejected with its own
reason and a log line. The rest pins D-008's limits: redirects only to
HTTPS and at most 3, and a size limit that holds however the server
frames the body (Content-Length, chunked, or until it closes, F-026).

- *certificate validation:* a file from a server with a valid certificate is fetched byte-identical (RFC [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
- *certificate validation:* a certificate for another host name is rejected and logged (RFC [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
- *certificate validation:* a certificate from a CA that isn't trusted is rejected and logged (RFC [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
- *certificate validation:* an expired certificate is rejected and logged (RFC [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
- *certificate validation:* a certificate that isn't valid yet is rejected and logged (RFC [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
- *certificate validation:* a URI with an IP address is rejected when the certificate only names a host (RFC [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
  A host given as an IP address must match the certificate too; a dNSName doesn't.
- *certificate validation:* by default only the system CA store is trusted (RFC [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
  Without :cacerts the system CA store is used, and it doesn't trust a test CA.
- *wildcard certificates (D-010):* a certificate that matches only by wildcard is accepted, logged and reported (RFC [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
  RFC 8630 §4: server names SHOULD NOT contain "*". The fetch succeeds,
  with a log line and a warning in the result. :address connects to
  127.0.0.1 while the name checked stays rpki.example.test.
- *wildcard certificates (D-010):* a certificate that also names the host exactly gives no warning
- *wildcard certificates (D-010):* a wildcard covers one label only (RFC [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
- *redirects (D-008):* a redirect to another HTTPS URI is followed, and the final URI reported
- *redirects (D-008):* a redirect to http:// is refused
- *redirects (D-008):* three redirects are followed, a fourth is refused
- *redirects (D-008):* a redirect to a URI Lumina doesn't accept is refused
  The target must pass Lumina.URI.parse/1, like any URI from a repository; a query doesn't.
- *size limit (D-008):* a body whose Content-Length is over the limit is refused
- *size limit (D-008):* a body sent until the server closes is cut off at the limit
  F-026: the case OTP's :httpc can't bound. The server just keeps sending.
- *size limit (D-008):* a chunked body over the limit is cut off
- *responses:* a chunked body is decoded
  RFC 9112 §7.1 chunked framing, which servers may use for any response.
- *responses:* a body that ends before its Content-Length is :truncated
- *responses:* a status other than 200 is :http_status
- *responses:* a response that isn't HTTP is :bad_response
- *connection failures:* a refused connection is :connection_refused
- *connection failures:* a host that doesn't resolve is :unknown_host
- *connection failures:* a server that never answers times out
  A server that accepts TCP and never starts TLS hits the connect timeout (D-008).

### `Lumina.LastValidTest`

[test/lumina/last_valid_test.exs](../../test/lumina/last_valid_test.exs)

Tests the last valid copy of publication points (#135, D-023):
`Lumina.LastValid` keeps an accepted point's manifest and listed files,
and `Lumina.Validate.point/5` falls back to that copy when the point
later fails, as long as its manifest is still current (RFC 9286 §6.6).

The publication points are fixture copies on disk (ca1's, caRepository
`rsync://localhost:8873/rpki/ca1`), changed between runs, at 2026-11-13
unless a test says otherwise.

- *LastValid:* an accepted point is saved as its manifest and listed files, once per manifest (RFC [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
- *LastValid:* saving the same manifest again leaves the copy alone; a new manifest replaces it
  Same manifest bytes, same files: nothing is copied again.
- *LastValid:* a point never accepted has no copy
- *falling back (D-023):* a point that fails uses its last valid copy, with a warning saying why (RFC [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
  roa1.roa changes, so its hash doesn't match: the saved copy is used instead.
- *falling back (D-023):* a last valid copy whose manifest is stale isn't used (RFC [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)), [9286 §6.3](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.3)))
  At 2036-06-01 the saved manifest is past its nextUpdate (2036-01-01).
- *falling back (D-023):* a point that never validated has no fallback (RFC [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
- *falling back (D-023):* without :save nothing is kept
  lumina validate reads the copies but never writes them (D-024's rule for state).

### `Lumina.M1DoneTest`

[test/lumina/m1_done_test.exs](../../test/lumina/m1_done_test.exs)

The end-to-end check that closes M1 (#33): every object in every Barry
fixture decodes through `Lumina.Object`, including the fixtures whose
objects break the RPKI profile (decoding is structural), and every
malformed variant built by `Lumina.Test.Mutate` is rejected at the DER
layer with the expected rule.

- every object in every fixture decodes as its type, including profile violations (RFC [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [6487 §4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4)), [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9286 §4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4)))
- every malformed variant of every fixture object is rejected at the DER layer (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)))
  Each mutation in Lumina.Test.Mutate breaks one DER rule. It's applied to
  every object it fits; certificates and CRLs have no signed attributes,
  so the signed-attribute mutation only applies to manifests and ROAs.
- inherited resources decode as :inherit, not as empty lists (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [3779 §3.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.3)))

### `Lumina.M2DoneTest`

[test/lumina/m2_done_test.exs](../../test/lumina/m2_done_test.exs)

The end-to-end check that closes M2, TAL parsing (#60). It runs every
TAL Lumina has against the whole M2 pipeline:

  * each Barry fixture's TAL parses, and its TA certificate passes
    `check_ta/2` unless the fixture's metadata says the TA is invalid;
  * each RIR TAL parses, prefers an HTTPS URI (D-003) and prints;
  * the test TAL corpus exercises every parser rule and gives its
    expected outcome;
  * RFC 8630 §2.2, §2.3, §2.4 and §3 are covered by tests other than
    this one.

The individual behaviours are tested in detail elsewhere (`TALTest`,
`TALCheckTest`, `TALURIOrderTest`, `TALRIRTest`, `PrintTest`). This
module checks that they hold together, over all the data at once.

- every Barry TA passes against its TAL exactly when its metadata says it should (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)), [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
  Driven by the fixture metadata: a fixture whose expected outcome names
  ta.cer as invalid must fail the TA check with one problem; every other
  fixture's TA must pass.
- every RIR TAL parses, is tried HTTPS first, and prints (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
  All five RIRs publish an HTTPS URI, so D-003 always starts with HTTPS on them.
- the test TAL corpus exercises every parser rule, each with its expected outcome (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
  Every error and warning rule the parser can report is the expected
  outcome of at least one corpus case, and the parser gives it there.
- RFC 8630 §2.2, §2.3, §2.4 and §3 are covered by other tests
  The coverage `mix lumina.rfc_coverage --rfc 8630` reports, computed the
  same way, ignoring this module's own tags.

### `Lumina.M3DoneTest`

[test/lumina/m3_done_test.exs](../../test/lumina/m3_done_test.exs)

The end-to-end check that closes M3, rsync retrieval (#77). It runs
`lumina sync` (`Lumina.CLI.run/4`) the way a user would, over the whole
M3 pipeline: TAL, TA retrieval (HTTPS first), repository walk, rsync,
cache.

  * Every Barry fixture is synced from a local HTTPS server and rsync
    daemon. The mirror must be byte-identical to the fixture's `rsync/`
    tree, the accepted TA identical to its `ta.cer`, and every mirrored
    object must decode (M1). Fixtures whose TA fails the TAL check
    must mirror nothing.
  * RFC 5781 §2, RFC 6481 §3 and §5, and RFC 8630 §3 and §4 are
    covered by tests other than this one.
  * Tagged `:network`, run by hand only (`mix test --only network`):
    the live LACNIC repository is mirrored from `tals/lacnic.tal`.

The individual behaviours are tested in detail elsewhere (`HTTPSTest`,
`RsyncTest`, `TATest`, `WalkTest`, `CLISyncTest`). This module checks
that they hold together, over all the data at once.

Fixture TALs name `https://localhost:8443` and `rsync://localhost:8873`.
Each fixture gets its own servers, a copy of its TAL pointing at them,
and `:remap` for the repository URIs inside its certificates.

- every Barry fixture syncs through lumina sync into a byte-identical mirror (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)), [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [6481 §3](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-3)), [5781 §2](../rfc/rfc5781.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5781.html#section-2)))
  Driven by the fixture metadata. A fixture whose TA is invalid exits 1
  with nothing mirrored. Every other fixture's TA arrives over HTTPS
  (D-003) and its whole repository over rsync. The delegated fixture's
  second host is served too; the unreachable fixtures exit 0 (only a
  delegated host fails, D-037, #187), with the rest mirrored.
- RFC 5781 §2, RFC 6481 §3 and §5, and RFC 8630 §3 and §4 are covered by other tests
  The coverage `mix lumina.rfc_coverage` reports, computed the same way,
  ignoring this module's own tags.
- *the live LACNIC repository:* the live LACNIC repository mirrors from tals/lacnic.tal and every object decodes (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)), [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  Run by hand: mix test --only network. Needs the Internet; takes
  minutes. Delegated repositories on other hosts may be down, so their
  failures are printed but don't fail the test; LACNIC's own
  repository and TA must arrive. In the local LACNIC copy of
  2026-11 the repository held about 28,000 files.
  ASPA objects (.asa) aren't decoded: ASPA isn't an RFC yet.

### `Lumina.M4DoneTest`

[test/lumina/m4_done_test.exs](../../test/lumina/m4_done_test.exs)

The end-to-end check that closes M4, certificates and CRLs (#115). It
runs `lumina sync` and then `lumina validate` (`Lumina.CLI.run/4`) the
way a user would, over the whole M4 pipeline: TA validation, the walk
through valid CAs, and offline validation of every CA and EE
certificate in the cache.

  * Every Barry fixture is synced from a local rsync daemon and
    validated at 2030-01-01, the time the chain and profile tests use.
    The certificates found invalid must be exactly those the fixture's
    `expected` metadata names with a `rule`, each rejected for that
    rule (since #131 that includes the CMS envelope of signed objects,
    the `m5-cms-*` fixtures); a fixture with nothing invalid must
    validate completely.
  * RFC 6487 §4, §5 and §7.2, RFC 7935 §2 and §3, and RFC 9829 §3 are
    covered by tests other than this one.
  * Tagged `:network`, run by hand only (`mix test --only network`):
    the live LACNIC repository is synced from `tals/lacnic.tal` and
    validated; the counts and every invalid certificate are printed.

The individual behaviours are tested in detail elsewhere (`ChainTest`,
`ProfileTest`, `WalkTest`, `CLIValidateTest`, ...). This module checks
that they hold together, over all the data at once.

- every Barry fixture syncs and validates to the verdicts its metadata states (RFC [6487 §4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4)), [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)), [7935 §3](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-3)), [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)), [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)))
  Driven by the fixture metadata. A fixture whose rejected TA has a
  rule: sync exits 1 naming the rule, and validate finds no TA. Every
  other fixture: sync and validate agree, the certificates validate
  finds invalid are exactly those the ruled rejects name (rejects
  without a rule are later milestones' checks or lie below an invalid
  CA), each for its rule, nothing fails to decode, and validate
  exits 1 exactly when something is invalid (each fixture's invalid
  share is above D-022's 10%).
- RFC 6487 §4, §5 and §7.2, RFC 7935 §2 and §3, and RFC 9829 §3 are covered by other tests
  The coverage `mix lumina.rfc_coverage` reports, computed the same way,
  ignoring this module's own tags. A section counts as covered by a
  test of it or of one of its subsections.
- *the live LACNIC repository:* the live LACNIC repository syncs and validates from tals/lacnic.tal (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  Run by hand: mix test --only network. Needs the Internet; takes
  minutes. Syncs LACNIC and validates the cache, printing the
  summary. Every CA certificate under LACNIC's own repository must
  validate; delegated repositories may hold faults (in 2026-11, 21
  expired manifests at one of them), printed but not failing the
  test as long as the share stays within D-022's 10%.

### `Lumina.M5DoneTest`

[test/lumina/m5_done_test.exs](../../test/lumina/m5_done_test.exs)

The end-to-end check that closes M5, signed objects and manifests
(#138). It runs `lumina sync` and then `lumina validate`
(`Lumina.CLI.run/4`) the way a user would, over the whole M5 pipeline:
the CMS envelope of every signed object (RFC 6488, RFC 9589), manifest
content (RFC 9286 §4), publication point processing (§6, RFC 9981), the
last valid copy (D-023) and replay protection (D-024).

  * Every Barry fixture is synced from a local rsync daemon and
    validated at 2030-01-01. Each publication point must be accepted or
    failed as the fixture's `expected` metadata states: it fails exactly
    when a reject with a `rule` names its manifest or its CRL. Nothing
    is validated below a failed point, every signed object of an
    accepted point is validated, and the signed objects found invalid
    are exactly those a ruled reject names. (`M4DoneTest` covers the certificates and the
    rejected TAs.)
  * Over one copy of a repository changed between syncs, a point that
    fails, live or as a replay, is served from its last valid copy by
    both commands.
  * RFC 6488 §3, RFC 9589 §4, RFC 9286 §4.2-4.4 and §6, and RFC 9981
    §2-4 are covered by tests other than this one.
  * Tagged `:network`, run by hand only (`mix test --only network`):
    the live LACNIC repository is synced and validated, and its
    publication points accepted, failed (with reasons) and served from
    the last valid copy are printed.

The individual behaviours are tested in detail elsewhere (`CMSTest`,
`ManifestCheckTest`, `PublicationPointTest`, `LastValidTest`,
`ManifestStateTest`, `WalkTest`, ...). This module checks that they hold
together, over all the data at once.

- every Barry fixture's publication points and signed objects get the verdicts its metadata states (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [9286 §4.4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.4)), [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
  Driven by the fixture metadata; fixtures whose TA is rejected are
  M4DoneTest's. A point fails exactly when a ruled reject names its
  manifest (its CMS envelope, its content, or the point's files) or
  its CRL (which invalidates the manifest's EE certificate). A
  failed point has only its manifest entry, nothing validated below
  it; an accepted point has an entry for every signed object it
  publishes, and those found invalid are exactly the ones a ruled
  reject names. The summary's manifest and ROA counts agree.
- a point that fails live or as a replay is served from its last valid copy by sync and validate (RFC [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)), [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  One copy of m0-minimal-valid, served by a daemon and changed between
  syncs. A ROA that no longer matches its hash, and then (restored) a
  manifest older than the one recorded, each make ca1's point fail;
  sync and validate both serve it from the copy the first sync saved,
  with its ROA still valid, and exit 0.
- RFC 6488 §3, RFC 9589 §4, RFC 9286 §4.2-4.4 and §6, and RFC 9981 §2-4 are covered by other tests
  The coverage `mix lumina.rfc_coverage` reports, computed the same way,
  ignoring this module's own tags. A section counts as covered by a
  test of it or of one of its subsections.
- *the live LACNIC repository:* the live LACNIC repository's publication points are processed (RFC [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)), [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  Run by hand: mix test --only network. Needs the Internet; takes
  minutes. Syncs LACNIC twice into one cache (the second sync can
  serve points from the copies the first saved) and validates it,
  printing the publication points accepted, failed with their
  reasons, and served from the last valid copy. Failures are
  expected to be very few: at most 1% of the points, none in
  LACNIC's own repository.

### `Lumina.M6DoneTest`

[test/lumina/m6_done_test.exs](../../test/lumina/m6_done_test.exs)

The end-to-end check that closes M6, resource inclusion (#156). It runs
`lumina sync` and then `lumina validate` (`Lumina.CLI.run/4`) the way a
user would, over the whole M6 pipeline: effective resources with
`inherit` resolved (#153, D-026), resource inclusion (RFC 6487 §7.2
point 6, #154, D-028), its reporting (#155) and the manifest EE
`inherit` warning (#157, D-029).

  * Every Barry fixture is synced from a local rsync daemon and
    validated at 2030-01-01. The M6 fixtures (`m6-overclaim-*`,
    `m6-inherit-*`, `m6-encompass-*`, `m6-mft-ee-*`) give the verdicts
    their metadata states: each overclaim is listed by both commands
    (sync for CA certificates only) with the resources outside its
    issuer's, counted on the `overclaims:` line, and nothing below an
    overclaiming CA is validated. No other fixture gets a
    `resources_not_encompassed` problem, and every valid CA's
    effective resources are within its issuer's.
  * RFC 6487 §7.1 and §7.2, RFC 3779 §2.2.3.5, §2.3, §3.2.3.3 and §3.3
    are covered by tests other than this one.
  * Tagged `:network`, run by hand only (`mix test --only network`):
    the live LACNIC repository is synced and validated, and every
    overclaiming certificate is printed with the resources outside its
    issuer's.

The individual behaviours are tested in detail elsewhere
(`EffectiveResourcesTest`, `ResourceSetTest`, `ResourceInclusionTest`,
`ManifestEEInheritTest`, `CLIValidateTest`, `CLISyncTest`, ...). This
module checks that they hold together, over all the data at once.
(`M4DoneTest` and `M5DoneTest` check every fixture's other verdicts.)

- the overclaim and inheritance fixtures get their verdicts, and resource checks reject nothing else (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §3.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.3)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
  Driven by the fixture metadata; fixtures whose TA is rejected are
  M4DoneTest's. For an M6 fixture: validate exits 1 exactly when it
  states a reject; each overclaiming certificate is listed by
  validate, and by sync when it is a CA certificate, as
  `resources_not_encompassed: <the reason without " not held by the
  issuer">`; both print `overclaims: N` with N the overclaims stated
  (sync: the CA certificates among them), or no such line; nothing
  under an overclaiming CA's directory is validated. For every
  fixture: the certificates validate finds overclaiming are exactly
  those an overclaim reject names, and every valid CA's effective
  resources are encompassed by its issuer's (the TA's own for ca1).
- inherited resources are resolved from the issuer, recursively, end to end (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [3779 §3.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.3)), [9286 §5.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-5.1)))
  The effective resources the inheritance fixtures state, as validate
  carries them down: m6-inherit-from-empty's ca2 inherits both
  address families and holds ca1's IPv4 and no IPv6 (D-026); m6-inherit-two-levels' ca3
  holds ca1's resources through ca2.
- RFC 6487 §7.1 and §7.2, RFC 3779 §2.2.3.5, §2.3, §3.2.3.3 and §3.3 are covered by other tests
  The coverage `mix lumina.rfc_coverage` reports, computed the same way,
  ignoring this module's own tags. A section counts as covered by a
  test of it or of one of its subsections.
- *the live LACNIC repository:* the live LACNIC repository's overclaiming certificates are reported (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
  Run by hand: mix test --only network. Needs the Internet; takes
  minutes. Syncs LACNIC and validates it, printing every
  overclaiming certificate with the resources outside its issuer's.
  Overclaims are expected to be none or very few: at most 0.1% of
  the certificates and signed objects, each one explained when the
  test is run. The summary's overclaims line agrees.

### `Lumina.ManifestCheckTest`

[test/lumina/manifest_check_test.exs](../../test/lumina/manifest_check_test.exs)

Tests the manifest content checks (#132): `Lumina.Manifest.check/1`
against RFC 9286 §4.2.1, §4.2.2 and §4.4. An invalid manifest is
treated as though no manifest were present (§4.4), which makes its
publication point fail (#133), so a false positive here would throw
away a whole publication point.

Every manifest of the positive fixtures must pass, and each `m5-mft-*`
fixture must fail with exactly its one rule. The edge cases (boundaries,
case sensitivity, registered extensions) are tested on a decoded
m0-minimal-valid manifest changed in memory.

- *fixtures:* every manifest of the positive Barry fixtures passes (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [9286 §4.2.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.2)), [9286 §4.4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.4)))
- *fixtures:* m5-mft-version-1: a manifest version other than 0 is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [9286 §4.4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.4)))
- *fixtures:* m5-mft-dates-reversed: thisUpdate after nextUpdate is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.4)))
- *fixtures:* m5-mft-number-too-large: a manifest number of 21 octets is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
- *fixtures:* m5-mft-hash-sha1: a file hash algorithm other than SHA-256 is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
- *fixtures:* m5-mft-name-bad-character: a file name with a character outside a-z A-Z 0-9 - _ is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.2)))
- *fixtures:* m5-mft-name-unregistered-extension: an extension outside the IANA registry is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.2)), [6481 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-7.2)))
- *fixtures:* m5-mft-name-duplicate: a file name listed twice is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [9286 §4.2.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.2)))
- *empty file list (#37):* m5-mft-empty-file-list decodes but is rejected as empty (RFC [9286 §7](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-7)))
  Verified erratum 7118 corrects the module's SIZE (0..MAX) to
  SIZE (1..MAX). The module is kept as published (F-001), so the
  manifest decodes, as a file and as a repository object.
- *empty file list (#37):* a manifest listing a single file is not empty (RFC [9286 §7](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-7)))
  Erratum 7118: SIZE (1..MAX), so one entry is enough.
- *time formats (#48):* a fractional-second thisUpdate decodes but is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [5280 §4.1.2.5.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.5.2)))
  F-019: RFC 9286 §4.2.1 imports the CRL field's constraints; for a
  GeneralizedTime field that means RFC 5280 §4.1.2.5.2, which forbids
  fractional seconds although DER allows them. Barry can't write a
  fraction, so the manifest is m0-minimal-valid's re-encoded.
- *time formats (#48):* a fractional-second nextUpdate is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [5280 §4.1.2.5.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.5.2)))
- *time formats (#48):* a GeneralizedTime dated before 2050 is not rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [5280 §5.1.2.4](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.4)))
  F-019: RFC 5280 §5.1.2.4 wants a CRL's thisUpdate as UTCTime through
  2049; a manifest's can only be GeneralizedTime, so that rule isn't
  applied.
- *dates and numbers:* thisUpdate equal to nextUpdate is rejected (RFC [9286 §4.4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.4)))
  "thisUpdate precedes nextUpdate": equal times don't.
- *dates and numbers:* manifest numbers 0 and 2^159-1 pass; -1 and 2^159 are rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
  20 octets hold 0..2^159-1 as a DER INTEGER, the CRLNumber range §4.2.1 points to.
- *file names:* every extension in the IANA registry is accepted (RFC [9286 §4.2.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.2)), [6481 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-7.2)))
  F-032: the IANA registry as of 2026-11-14, temporary (.asa, .cdr)
  and deprecated (.gbr) entries included. LACNIC's manifests list
  .asa files.
- *file names:* names are case-sensitive (RFC [9286 §4.2.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.2)))
  Case-sensitive (§4.2.2): .ROA is not a registered extension, and A.roa is not a.roa.
- *file names:* names without a base, with two dots, a path, or a long extension are rejected (RFC [9286 §4.2.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.2)))
- *file names:* a name listed three times is one problem (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))

### `Lumina.ManifestEEInheritTest`

[test/lumina/manifest_ee_inherit_test.exs](../../test/lumina/manifest_ee_inherit_test.exs)

Tests the RFC 9286 §5.1 check on a manifest's EE certificate (#157):
it "MUST describe its Internet Number Resources (INRs) using the
'inherit' attribute, rather than an explicit description of a resource
set (see [RFC3779]). (RPs are required to verify this.)"

`Lumina.PublicationPoint.process/5` warns
`manifest_ee_resources_not_inherit` once, naming each kind (IPv4, IPv6,
AS numbers) the EE certificate lists explicitly. It is a warning, not
an error, while Barry writes explicit resources on every manifest it
isn't told about (D-029); a kind left out doesn't warn (D-029). Barry's
default manifests warn naming all three kinds, `m6-mft-ee-inherit`'s ca1
manifest inherits every kind, and `m6-mft-ee-explicit-ipv4`'s lists
IPv4, leaves IPv6 out and inherits AS numbers. Points are processed at
2030-01-01.

- *PublicationPoint.process/5:* a manifest EE certificate listing every kind explicitly warns once, naming them, and the point is accepted (RFC [9286 §5.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-5.1)))
  Barry writes explicit IPv4, IPv6 and AS numbers on manifests it isn't told about.
- *PublicationPoint.process/5:* m6-mft-ee-inherit: a manifest EE certificate inheriting every kind gets no warning (RFC [9286 §5.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-5.1)), [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [3779 §3.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.3)))
- *PublicationPoint.process/5:* m6-mft-ee-explicit-ipv4: only the kind listed explicitly warns (RFC [9286 §5.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-5.1)))
- *PublicationPoint.process/5:* a kind the manifest EE certificate leaves out doesn't warn (RFC [9286 §5.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-5.1)))
  D-029: m6-mft-ee-explicit-ipv4's manifest has no IPv6 at all. §5.1
  asks for inherit "rather than an explicit description", and an
  absent kind describes nothing; RFC 6487 §4.8.10 lets a
  certificate leave a family out.
- *lumina validate:* the warning is shown on the manifest's line, and doesn't change the exit code (RFC [9286 §5.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-5.1)))

### `Lumina.ManifestStateTest`

[test/lumina/manifest_state_test.exs](../../test/lumina/manifest_state_test.exs)

Tests manifest replay protection across runs (#136, D-024):
`Lumina.ManifestState` and its use in `Lumina.Validate.point/5`.

RFC 9286 §4.2.1 requires a new manifest to have a higher number and a
more recent thisUpdate than the last one validated; RFC 9981 §2-3 resets
the number check when the manifest's file name changes. Barry generates
fresh keys for every fixture, so two fixtures never share a CA; instead,
the record of "the last manifest validated" is written ahead of
m0-minimal-valid's ca1 manifest (number 1, thisUpdate 2026-01-01),
which then plays the replayed, older manifest.

- *recording:* a sync records the accepted manifest; seeing the same one again is fine (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
- *recording:* a 20-octet manifest number round-trips
  Numbers up to 20 octets survive the JSON record.
- *recording:* only an accepted point with :save is recorded
  lumina validate (no :save) and a fallback point never move the record (D-024).
- *replays (RFC 9286 §4.2.1):* a manifest number lower than the last one validated fails the point (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
- *replays (RFC 9286 §4.2.1):* an equal manifest number on a different manifest fails the point (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
  Same number, another thisUpdate: a different manifest.
- *replays (RFC 9286 §4.2.1):* a higher number with an older thisUpdate fails the point (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
- *replays (RFC 9286 §4.2.1):* a replayed manifest falls back to the last valid copy, and the record stays (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
  The replayed manifest is a failed fetch, so the copy the sync kept stands in (D-023).
- *file name changes (RFC 9981):* a new manifest file name skips the number check, with a warning (RFC [9981 §2](../rfc/rfc9981.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9981.html#section-2)), [9981 §3](../rfc/rfc9981.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9981.html#section-3)))
  The number check is reset; operators are alerted with a warning.
- *file name changes (RFC 9981):* a new manifest file name with an older thisUpdate still fails (RFC [9981 §2](../rfc/rfc9981.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9981.html#section-2)), [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
  RFC 9981 §2: with the number check reset, the thisUpdate check still protects.

### `Lumina.ManifestTest`

[test/lumina/manifest_test.exs](../../test/lumina/manifest_test.exs)

Tests decoding of manifests (RFC 9286). Publication point validation (M5)
compares each file against the manifest's hash and checks the manifest
number and times, so these must decode exactly. Decoding is structural:
an empty file list decodes, and its rejection is validation's job (#37).

- *the m0-minimal-valid manifests:* list exactly the other files in their publication points (RFC [9286 §4.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2)), [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)))
  Each manifest lists every other file at its publication point; the manifest itself is not listed.
- *the m0-minimal-valid manifests:* each listed hash is the SHA-256 of the file (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
  Decode sanity only: each listed hash equals the SHA-256 of the file. Checking it is M5.
- *the m0-minimal-valid manifests:* version, manifest number, times and hash algorithm (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
- *structural decoding:* an empty file list decodes to no files (RFC [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt), [9286 §7](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-7)))
  The module allows SIZE (0..MAX). Verified erratum 7118 and §7 forbid an
  empty list, but rejecting it is M5's job (#37, F-001), so it must decode.
- *structural decoding:* a 20-octet manifest number decodes exactly (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
  Manifest numbers up to 20 octets MUST be processable.
- *structural decoding:* a non-zero version decodes with that version (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
- *structural decoding:* an explicitly encoded default version is not DER (RFC [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt))
  X.690 11.5: version [0] equal to its DEFAULT 0 must not be encoded; only re-encoding catches it.
- *structural decoding:* a time that isn't a real date is an error
- *errors:* a signed object that isn't a manifest
- *errors:* non-DER and unparseable eContent

### `Lumina.ObjectTest`

[test/lumina/object_test.exs](../../test/lumina/object_test.exs)

Tests the entry point that decodes any repository file by its extension.
Repository processing and `lumina --print` go through it, so every
registered extension must reach the right decoder, a signed object's
eContent type must agree with its extension, and failures must name the
layer that failed.

- every file in every fixture decodes as the type its extension names (RFC [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)), [6481 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-7.2)))
- registered extensions map to their types; others are unknown (RFC [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)), [6493 §9.2](../rfc/rfc6493.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6493.html#section-9.2)), [9323 §9.3](../rfc/rfc9323.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9323.html#section-9.3)), [9691 §11.3](../rfc/rfc9691.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9691.html#section-11.3)))
- a signed object whose eContent type disagrees with its extension is rejected (RFC [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)), [6488 §2.1.3.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.3.1)))
  A manifest published under a .roa name must not be taken for a ROA.
- Ghostbusters, RSC and TAK objects decode their envelope only (RFC [6493 §9.2](../rfc/rfc6493.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6493.html#section-9.2)), [9323 §9.3](../rfc/rfc9323.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9323.html#section-9.3)), [9691 §11.3](../rfc/rfc9691.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9691.html#section-11.3)))
  Ghostbusters, RSC and TAK eContent is decoded in M9; until then the envelope is decoded and eContent kept raw.
- *errors name the layer:* DER
- *errors name the layer:* ASN.1
- *errors name the layer:* envelope
- *errors name the layer:* eContent
- *errors name the layer:* type and file

### `Lumina.PrintTest`

[test/lumina/print_test.exs](../../test/lumina/print_test.exs)

Tests the human-readable rendering behind `lumina print` (#34), full and
`--brief` (D-001 in doc/decisions.md). Expected
values come from the decoded structs, not hard-coded bytes, so
regenerating a fixture (fresh keys) doesn't break the tests. The output
must be stable: the same file always prints the same text.

- a CA certificate prints its fields, extensions and resources
- the TA certificate is marked self-issued
- printing the same file twice gives identical text
- a ROA prints its envelope, EE certificate and prefixes with max lengths
- a manifest prints its number, times and each file with its hash
- a CRL prints its dates, revocations and CRL number
- an unknown extension prints its OID, criticality and hex (RFC [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)))
- inherited resources print as inherit
- profile violations print like anything else
- a signed object whose eContent isn't decoded yet prints its envelope and size
- *brief:* a brief certificate keeps names, validity, URIs and resources, and drops crypto detail
- *brief:* a brief manifest lists file names without hashes
- *brief:* a brief ROA keeps the signing time, EE validity and prefixes
- *brief:* a brief CRL keeps issuer, dates, number and revocations
- *brief:* brief still shows unknown extensions, without their bytes (RFC [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)))
- *brief:* inherit is kept in brief output
- *TALs (#59):* a Barry TAL prints its URIs and the SKI its TA certificate actually carries (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)))
  The printed SKI is the one `check_ta/2` compares, so it must match the
  TA certificate Barry generated for the same key (RFC 6487 §4.8.2).
- *TALs (#59):* the RFC 8630 example prints in full (RFC [8630 §2.4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.4)))
  The whole printout is pinned, so a change to the layout is deliberate.
  The preference order follows D-003: HTTPS first, though the TAL lists
  rsync first.
- *TALs (#59):* brief leaves out the key and keeps the comments, URIs and SKI (RFC [8630 §2.4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.4)))
- *TALs (#59):* parser warnings print with their line numbers (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
  Warnings (D-002) are kept in brief output: they say the file isn't clean.
- *TALs (#59):* a TAL parse error names the line, the rule and the RFC section (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
- *error/2:* names the layer for each kind of failure

### `Lumina.ProductionTALsTest`

[test/lumina/production_tals_test.exs](../../test/lumina/production_tals_test.exs)

The production TALs in `tals/` (D-004, #67). They must be byte-exact
copies of the reviewed RIR TALs in `test/fixtures/tals/rir/`, which
`Lumina.TALRIRTest` checks in detail, so production never uses a TAL
that wasn't approved and tested. They must also parse cleanly where they
are, under the strict grammar (D-002).

- tals/ holds the same five TAL files as the reviewed RIR TALs
  Adding or removing a TAL in one folder and not the other fails.
- every production TAL is byte-identical to its reviewed copy
  Byte for byte: a changed key, URI, line ending or comment in either copy fails.
- every production TAL parses with no warnings (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))

### `Lumina.ProfileCRLTest`

[test/lumina/profile_crl_test.exs](../../test/lumina/profile_crl_test.exs)

Tests the CRL profile (`Lumina.Profile.crl/3`, #111): RFC 6487 §5 as
updated by RFC 9829 §3.1, with the CRL's signature checked against the
issuing CA's key.

Every CRL of the positive Barry fixtures must pass, and each `m4-crl-*`
fixture breaks one rule; `m4-crl-stale` is accepted with a `stale_crl`
warning (D-016). Cases Barry can't produce (revoked entries, #52) change
one field of a decoded fixture CRL; the signature covers the unchanged
`tbs_der`, so it still verifies.

Fixtures validate at 2030-01-01.

- *fixtures:* every CRL of every positive Barry fixture passes (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)), [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)))
  Each CRL checked with the certificate of the CA it belongs to.
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-version-1: a version 1 CRL is rejected (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)))
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-extra-extension: a third extension is rejected (RFC [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)))
  Unlike in certificates (D-013), a non-critical unknown extension rejects a CRL.
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-number-critical: a critical CRL Number is rejected (RFC [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)))
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-number-too-large: a CRL Number of 2^159 is rejected (RFC [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)))
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-number-negative: a negative CRL Number is rejected (RFC [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)))
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-aki-mismatch: an AKI other than the issuer's key identifier is rejected (RFC [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)), [5280 §5.2.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.2.1)))
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-issuer-mismatch: a CRL whose issuer isn't the CA's subject is rejected (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)))
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-bad-signature: a CRL whose signature doesn't verify is rejected (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [8017 §8.2.2](../rfc/rfc8017.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8017.html#section-8.2.2)))
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-stale: a CRL past its nextUpdate is accepted with a stale_crl warning (RFC [5280 §5.1.2.5](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.5)))
  D-016: a stale CRL is still used.
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-name-extra-attribute: a CRL whose issuer name breaks §4.4 is rejected (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)), [6487 §4.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.4)))
- *fixtures:* m1-cert-no-ski: the CRL of a CA without an SKI still matches its AKI (RFC [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)), [6487 §4.8.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.3)))
  The AKI is compared with the SHA-1 of the issuer's key, not with its SKI extension.
- *dates:* a CRL is stale only after its nextUpdate (RFC [5280 §5.1.2.5](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.5)))
- *dates:* a CRL before its thisUpdate is rejected (RFC [5280 §5.1.2.4](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.4)))
- *dates:* a CRL without nextUpdate is rejected (RFC [5280 §5.1.2.5](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.5)))
- *extensions:* a CRL without an AKI or without a CRL Number is rejected (RFC [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)))
- *extensions:* an extension that appears twice is rejected (RFC [5280 §4.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.2)))
- *extensions:* CRL Numbers 0 and 2^159-1 are accepted (RFC [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)))
  0 and 2^159-1 are the bounds RFC 9829 allows.
- *entries and algorithms:* a revoked entry with extensions is rejected; one without is accepted (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)))
  Barry can't write revoked entries (#52), so the decoded entry list is changed.
- *entries and algorithms:* a tbsCertList algorithm unlike the outer one is rejected (RFC [5280 §5.1.1.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.1.2)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))

### `Lumina.ProfileExtensionsTest`

[test/lumina/profile_extensions_test.exs](../../test/lumina/profile_extensions_test.exs)

Tests the extension checks of the resource certificate profile
(`Lumina.Profile.extensions/2`, #110): RFC 6487 §4.8, as updated by
RFC 7318, for TA, CA and EE certificates.

Every certificate of the positive Barry fixtures must pass the whole
profile (`certificate/3`), and each `m4-cert-*` extension fixture, plus
`m1-cert-no-ski` and `m1-cert-unknown-critical-extension`, breaks one
rule. `m4-cert-unknown-extension` is valid with one warning (D-013,
#42). Cases Barry can't produce (it can't set the certificatePolicies
value, F-030) change one extension of a decoded fixture certificate;
the profile checks don't verify signatures, so it needn't be re-signed.

- *fixtures:* every certificate of every positive Barry fixture passes the whole profile (RFC [6487 §4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4)), [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)))
  TA, CA and EE certificates (from manifests and ROAs) of every
  fixture expected valid; m4-cert-unknown-extension passes with a
  warning, the others without any problem.
- *fixtures:* m1-cert-no-ski: a certificate without a Subject Key Identifier is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.2)))
- *fixtures:* m1-cert-unknown-critical-extension: an unknown critical extension is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-unknown-extension: an unknown non-critical extension is accepted with a warning (RFC [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)), [5280 §4.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.2)))
  D-013, #42: accepted, with a warning that names the OID.
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-ca-no-basic-constraints: a CA certificate without Basic Constraints is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.1)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-key-usage-not-critical: a non-critical Key Usage is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.4)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-ca-eku: an Extended Key Usage in a CA certificate is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.5)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-sia-no-manifest: a CA certificate whose SIA has no rpkiManifest is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.1)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-no-resources: a certificate with neither IP nor AS resources is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)), [6487 §4.8.11](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.11)))
- *general rules:* an extension that appears twice is rejected (RFC [5280 §4.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.2)))
- *general rules:* a profile extension whose value doesn't decode is rejected as malformed (RFC [5280 §4.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.2)))
- *general rules:* a known extension outside the certificate profile is handled like an unknown one (RFC [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)))
  A CRL extension is known to Lumina but has no place in a certificate.
- *basic constraints, key identifiers, key usage:* an EE certificate with Basic Constraints is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.1)))
- *basic constraints, key identifiers, key usage:* a CA certificate with a path length constraint or without cA is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.1)))
- *basic constraints, key identifiers, key usage:* a Subject Key Identifier that isn't the SHA-1 of the key is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.2)))
- *basic constraints, key identifiers, key usage:* a CA certificate without an Authority Key Identifier is rejected; a TA may omit it (RFC [6487 §4.8.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.3)))
- *basic constraints, key identifiers, key usage:* a TA whose Authority Key Identifier differs from its SKI is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.3)))
- *basic constraints, key identifiers, key usage:* an Authority Key Identifier with authorityCertSerialNumber is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.3)))
- *basic constraints, key identifiers, key usage:* Key Usage bits other than the kind's are rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.4)))
- *basic constraints, key identifiers, key usage:* an Extended Key Usage in the EE certificate of a signed object is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.5)))
  A well-formed EKU (id-kp-bgpsec-router) on the EE certificate of a ROA.
- *CRLDP, AIA and SIA:* a self-signed certificate with a CRLDP or an AIA is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.6](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.6)), [6487 §4.8.7](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.7)))
- *CRLDP, AIA and SIA:* a CA certificate without a CRLDP or an AIA is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.6](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.6)), [6487 §4.8.7](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.7)))
- *CRLDP, AIA and SIA:* a CRLDP with two DistributionPoints, a cRLIssuer or no rsync URI is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.6](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.6)))
- *CRLDP, AIA and SIA:* an AIA without an rsync caIssuers URI is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.7](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.7)))
- *CRLDP, AIA and SIA:* an EE certificate's SIA with an access method other than signedObject is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.2)))
- *CRLDP, AIA and SIA:* an rpkiNotify in an EE certificate's SIA only warns (RFC [6487 §4.8.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.2)))
  AFRINIC's EE certificates carry it, following RFC 8182 §3.2 as
  published; erratum 7239 says only CA certificates must (D-038, TD-002).
- *CRLDP, AIA and SIA:* an EE certificate's SIA with rpkiNotify and another extra method is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.2)))
- *CRLDP, AIA and SIA:* a CA certificate's SIA without an rsync caRepository is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.1)))
- *CRLDP, AIA and SIA:* a critical SIA is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.1)))
- *certificate policies (RFC 7318):* a policy other than the RPKI CP is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.9](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.9)))
  F-030: Barry can't write this, so the decoded value is changed.
