- *certificate policies (RFC 7318):* the RFC 8360 policy is rejected as unsupported (RFC [6487 §4.8.9](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.9)))
  RFC 8360's policy needs the v2 resource extensions, which Lumina doesn't support.
- *certificate policies (RFC 7318):* two policies are rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.9](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.9)))
- *certificate policies (RFC 7318):* one CPS pointer qualifier is accepted, any other qualifier is rejected (RFC [7318 §2](../rfc/rfc7318.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7318.html#section-2)))
- *certificate policies (RFC 7318):* non-critical certificate policies are rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.9](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.9)))
- *resources:* IP resources with a SAFI are rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)))
- *resources:* AS resources with RDIs are rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.11](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.11)))
- *resources:* an empty resource set is rejected, and inherit is accepted (RFC [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)), [6487 §4.8.11](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.11)))
- *resources:* non-critical resource extensions are rejected (RFC [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)), [6487 §4.8.11](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.11)))
- *resources:* one resource extension is enough (RFC [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)))
  An EE certificate of a ROA carries IP resources only.

### `Lumina.ProfileTest`

[test/lumina/profile_test.exs](../../test/lumina/profile_test.exs)

Tests the basic-field checks of the resource certificate profile
(`Lumina.Profile.basic_fields/2`, #109): RFC 6487 §4.1 to §4.7, with the
validity check of §7.2.

Every certificate of the positive Barry fixtures must pass, and each
`m4-cert-*` fixture (plus `m1-cert-version-2`) breaks one rule, which
must be the one reported. Cases Barry can't produce, such as unique
identifiers or a commonName that isn't a PrintableString, change one
field of a decoded fixture certificate; the profile checks don't verify
signatures, so the struct needn't be re-signed.

Fixtures validate at 2030-01-01, inside the default 2026-2036
validity.

- *fixtures:* every certificate of every positive Barry fixture passes (RFC [6487 §4.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.1)), [6487 §4.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.2)), [6487 §4.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.3)), [6487 §4.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.4)), [6487 §4.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.5)), [6487 §4.6](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.6)), [6487 §4.7](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.7)))
  TA, CA and EE certificates (from manifests and ROAs) of every fixture expected valid.
- *fixtures:* m1-cert-version-2: a version 2 certificate is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.1)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-expired: a certificate past its notAfter is rejected as expired (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-not-yet-valid: a certificate before its notBefore is rejected (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-serial-zero: serial number 0 is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.2)), [5280 §4.1.2.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.2)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-serial-negative: a negative serial number is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.2)), [5280 §4.1.2.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.2)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-serial-too-long: a 21-octet serial number is rejected (RFC [5280 §4.1.2.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.2)))
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-inner-signature-algorithm: an inner algorithm unlike the outer one is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.3)), [5280 §4.1.1.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.1.2)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
  sha384WithRSAEncryption inside: both a mismatch and an unsupported algorithm.
- *fixtures:* m4-cert-name-extra-attribute: a name with an organizationName is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.4)), [6487 §4.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.5)))
  The CA's subject, and the issuer of the EE certificates it signs.
- *validity:* a certificate is valid at exactly its notBefore and its notAfter (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  notBefore and notAfter are both inside the validity period.
- *serial number:* a 20-octet serial number is accepted (RFC [5280 §4.1.2.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.2)))
  2^159 - 1 is the largest positive INTEGER in 20 octets.
- *names:* a commonName with a serialNumber is accepted (RFC [6487 §4.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.5)))
- *names:* a commonName that isn't a PrintableString is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.5)))
- *names:* a name without a commonName is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.5)))
- *names:* a name with two commonNames is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.5)))
- *names:* a name with two serialNumbers is rejected (RFC [6487 §4.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.5)))
- *fields the profile excludes:* issuer and subject unique identifiers are rejected (RFC [6487 §4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4)))
  RFC 6487 §4: fields not listed in the profile MUST NOT appear.
- *public key (D-018):* a sha256WithRSAEncryption key algorithm is accepted with a warning (RFC [7935 §3.1](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-3.1)), [4055 §1.2](../rfc/rfc4055.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4055.html#section-1.2)))
  F-027: allowed by RFC 7935 §3.1's text, not by practice; a warning, so it passes.
- *public key (D-018):* a 1024-bit key is rejected (RFC [7935 §3](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-3)))

### `Lumina.ProgressTest`

[test/lumina/progress_test.exs](../../test/lumina/progress_test.exs)

Tests progress reporting (`Lumina.Progress`, #96): the events a walk
emits, the status text built from a scripted event sequence, and
`lumina sync --progress` / `--quiet`. Validation reports progress too
(#180): `Lumina.Validate.run/3`'s events and `lumina validate` /
`lumina vrps` with `--progress` / `--quiet`. Every long-running
operation reports progress (D-036).

Progress goes to stderr and never changes stdout. It is on by default
(D-036): tests run with StringIO devices, which aren't terminals, so
the commands report timestamped lines unless given `--quiet`. Other
test modules add `--quiet` (`Lumina.Test.Quiet`); these run the
commands as given.

- *events:* a walk emits level and fetch events, in order, with outcomes and file counts
  m0-minimal-valid: the TA's level fetches the module rpki (all 7
  files), which already holds ca1's publication point, so the next
  level fetches nothing. Each level is started, its fetches run, and
  it is finished, with the running totals of the walk.
- *events:* emit/2 without a listener does nothing
- *status text:* the TA being tried shows before the walk starts
- *status text:* a walk in progress shows its level, points, rsync runs and files
- *status text:* a fetch running for more than 5 s is shown as the slowest, with its host
  A stuck host (like krill.dacs.utwente.nl in the live LACNIC run) becomes visible.
- *status text:* on a terminal, the status line is cut to the terminal width
- *validation (#180):* Validate.run/3 reports each level and each point validated, with counts matching the result
  m0-minimal-valid, synced then validated: a level event pair per
  level, and one point_validated per publication point whose
  objects and invalid counts add up to the result's.
- *validation (#180):* a validation in progress shows its level, points, objects and invalid ones
- *validation (#180):* lumina validate and lumina vrps report progress on stderr by default, and stdout is unchanged
  Without any flag, and with --progress, the same timestamped lines
  (StringIO isn't a terminal); stdout is what --quiet gives.
- *validation (#180):* --quiet reports no progress for lumina validate and lumina vrps
- *validation (#180):* lumina help validate and lumina help vrps list --progress and --quiet
- *lumina sync:* progress is reported by default, as plain timestamped lines, and stdout is unchanged
  StringIO isn't a terminal, so these are the plain lines a log or a
  pipe gets: a timestamp, no control characters, one line per TAL
  and per finished level.
- *lumina sync:* --quiet reports no progress
- *lumina sync:* lumina help sync lists --progress and --quiet

### `Lumina.PublicationPointTest`

[test/lumina/publication_point_test.exs](../../test/lumina/publication_point_test.exs)

Tests publication point processing (#133): `Lumina.PublicationPoint.process/4`
decides from a fixture's files whether a CA's publication point can be
used (RFC 9286 §6, RFC 9981 §4).

A point is ca1's (`rsync/ca1`, caRepository
`rsync://localhost:8873/rpki/ca1`) unless a test says otherwise, at
2030-01-01, inside the fixtures' validity. Every positive fixture's
points must be accepted with exactly the manifest's files, and each
`m5-pp-*` fixture must fail with exactly its reasons. Cases Barry can't
publish (a missing or undecodable manifest, an extra file) work on a
copy of m0-minimal-valid changed on disk.

- *fixtures:* every positive Barry fixture's publication points are accepted with exactly the manifest's files (RFC [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)), [9286 §6.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.2)), [9286 §6.3](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.3)), [9286 §6.4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.4)), [9286 §6.5](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.5)))
  The TA's point and ca1's (where it exists); warnings are allowed.
- *fixtures:* m5-pp-manifest-stale: a manifest past its nextUpdate fails the point (RFC [9286 §6.3](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.3)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
- *fixtures:* m5-pp-manifest-premature: a manifest before its thisUpdate fails the point (RFC [9286 §6.3](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.3)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
- *fixtures:* m5-pp-file-missing: a listed file that isn't published fails the point (RFC [9286 §6.4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.4)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
- *fixtures:* m5-pp-hash-mismatch: a file whose hash differs from the manifest's fails the point (RFC [9286 §6.5](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.5)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
- *fixtures:* m5-pp-crl-renamed: the CA's CRL not on the manifest, and a listed file missing, fail the point (RFC [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)), [9286 §6.4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.4)))
- *fixtures:* the CRL the manifest's EE certificate names must be on the manifest (RFC [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)), [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)))
  With ca2.crl published, the CRL rule stays: the CRL the CRLDP names
  (ca1.crl) isn't listed. The hash mismatch is Barry's: it writes an
  empty hash for a renamed entry (doc/barry.md).
- *fixtures:* m5-pp-manifest-revoked: a manifest whose EE certificate is revoked fails the point (RFC [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)), [9286 §6.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.2)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
- *fixtures:* m5-pp-manifest-sia-mismatch: a manifest whose signedObject URI isn't its own fails the point (RFC [9981 §4](../rfc/rfc9981.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9981.html#section-4)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
- *fixtures:* m5-mft-version-1: an invalid manifest fails the point with the manifest's own rule (RFC [9286 §6.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.2)), [9286 §4.4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.4)))
  An invalid manifest is treated as though no manifest were present (§4.4).
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-version-1: an invalid CRL fails the point (RFC [9286 §6.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.2)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  The manifest's EE certificate can't validate without a valid CRL.
- *fixtures:* m4-crl-stale: a stale CRL is accepted with a warning (RFC [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)))
  D-016: a stale CRL on a current manifest only warns.
- *on disk:* a missing manifest fails the point (RFC [9286 §6.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.2)))
- *on disk:* a manifest that doesn't decode fails the point (RFC [9286 §6.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.2)))
- *on disk:* a manifest outside the CA's publication point fails it (RFC [9286 §6.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.1)))
  The CA's caRepository is taken to be elsewhere, so its manifest URI is outside it.
- *on disk:* a file not on the manifest is left out of an accepted point (RFC [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)))
  Files not on the manifest "MUST NOT be used": they aren't in the result.
- *the CRL on the manifest (RFC 9829, #116):* m5-pp-crl-hash-mismatch: a manifest hash for the CRL that doesn't match fails the point (RFC [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)), [9829 §5](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-5)), [9286 §6.5](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.5)))
- *the CRL on the manifest (RFC 9829, #116):* a certificate whose CRL isn't on the manifest is invalid with crl_not_on_manifest (RFC [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)))
  Barry can't give one certificate a CRLDP of its own, so the point is
  m0-minimal-valid's, accepted, with ca1.crl taken off its file list:
  a CRL in the directory that the manifest doesn't list.
- *the CRL on the manifest (RFC 9829, #116):* a CRL that is neither listed nor published is missing (RFC [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
- *read_crl/3:* reads the CRL a URI names in the point, and nothing outside it (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  D-015: only the publication point's own CRL is read.

### `Lumina.ResourceInclusionTest`

[test/lumina/resource_inclusion_test.exs](../../test/lumina/resource_inclusion_test.exs)

Tests resource inclusion (#154): `Lumina.Chain.child/6` rejects a CA or
EE certificate whose effective resources aren't encompassed by its
issuer's (RFC 6487 §7.2 point 6; RFC 3779 §2.3 and §3.3: "Validation
MUST fail when this is not the case"), with rule
`resources_not_encompassed` and a message naming the resources outside.

The comparison itself (sets, kinds separately, D-027) is
`EncompassTest`'s. Here: the rule in the chain, through in-memory
changes to m0-minimal-valid's ca1 (an IP address range, which Barry
can't write in a certificate) and through the `m6-overclaim-*`
fixtures, one per way of overclaiming, at 2030-01-01; that an
overclaim deep in a chain invalidates only that branch (over rsync,
with `Lumina.Validate.run/3`); and that equal or inherited resources
stay valid. The certificate is invalid as a whole: RFC 8360 isn't
applied (#121).

- *Chain.child/6:* a certificate holding addresses outside its issuer's is invalid, naming them (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
  ca1 holds 1.0.0.0/8, 100::/8 and an AS range; the issuer is
  given as holding 1.0.0.0/9 and the rest, so ca1's upper half of
  1.0.0.0/8 lies outside. Only that is reported, as a prefix.
- *Chain.child/6:* an address range partly outside the issuer's is reported as the range outside (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
  Barry writes only prefixes in certificates, so the address range
  is set in memory: 1.0.0.0-1.0.1.9 against an issuer holding
  1.0.0.0/24. The part outside, 1.0.1.0-1.0.1.9, isn't a prefix and
  is shown as a range.
- *Chain.child/6:* resources outside in several kinds are all named in one problem (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
  IPv4, then IPv6, then AS numbers, in one message.
- *Chain.child/6:* a certificate holding exactly its issuer's resources is encompassed (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  Without a CRL the result is invalid for other reasons; only point 6 is checked.
- *Chain.child/6:* a certificate inheriting every kind is encompassed by any issuer (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)))
  Inherited kinds are the issuer's set, so they never lie outside,
  even when the issuer holds none of a kind (D-026).
- *fixtures:* m6-overclaim-ipv4: a CA claiming an IPv4 prefix outside its issuer's is invalid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
- *fixtures:* m6-overclaim-ipv6: a CA claiming an IPv6 prefix outside its issuer's is invalid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
- *fixtures:* m6-overclaim-as: a CA claiming an AS number outside its issuer's is invalid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
- *fixtures:* m6-overclaim-as-range: a CA claiming an AS range partly outside its issuer's is invalid, naming the part outside (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
- *fixtures:* m6-overclaim-ipv4-partial: a CA claiming a prefix that contains its issuer's is invalid, naming the part outside (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
- *fixtures:* m6-overclaim-family: a CA claiming an address family its issuer doesn't have is invalid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
- *fixtures:* m6-overclaim-roa-ee: a ROA whose EE certificate overclaims is invalid (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
- *fixtures:* m6-encompass-equal: a CA holding exactly its issuer's resources is valid (RFC [6487 §7.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.1)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.3)))
- *fixtures:* m6-inherit-two-levels: certificates inheriting everything are encompassed (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [3779 §3.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.3)))
- *a branch below an overclaim:* an overclaim deep in a chain invalidates only that certificate and what is below it (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [3779 §2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.3)))
  m6-overclaim-grandchild, synced from a local rsync daemon and
  validated offline: ca3 claims a prefix ca1 holds but ca2, its
  issuer, doesn't. ca3 is invalid, its publication point is never
  processed (no manifest entry, roa1 not reached), and its
  sibling ca4 and everything else validate.

### `Lumina.ResourcesTest`

[test/lumina/resources_test.exs](../../test/lumina/resources_test.exs)

Tests decoding of the RFC 3779 IP address and AS identifier extensions,
which resource-inclusion checks (M4/M6) depend on. Test vectors come from
the RFC's own worked examples (§2.1, §2.2.3.8, §2.2.3.9, Appendices B
and C), corrected where a verified erratum says the RFC is wrong
(erratum 6792, F-002 in doc/rfc-findings.md). The canonical-form checks
report violations without rejecting, because rejection belongs to
validation.

- *RFC 3779 Appendix B:* the first example decodes to the prefixes and range the RFC lists, in canonical form (RFC [3779 §B](../rfc/rfc3779.txt), [3779 §2.2.3.6](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.6)))
- *RFC 3779 Appendix B:* the second example, as corrected by erratum 6792, decodes to the stated prefixes (RFC [3779 §B](../rfc/rfc3779.txt))
  The second example as corrected by verified erratum 6792: the IPv4
  prefix 172.16/12 is ac10, not b010 as printed, and the IPv6 prefix is
  /48, not /47 as annotated. The family with SAFI 2 (multicast) inherits.
- *RFC 3779 Appendix B:* the second example's bytes as printed decode to 176.16/12 (RFC [3779 §B](../rfc/rfc3779.txt))
  Why the erratum matters: the bytes as printed in the RFC encode 176.16/12, not 172.16/12.
- *RFC 3779 Appendix C:* the AS example decodes to AS135, AS3000-AS3999, AS5001 and inherited RDIs (RFC [3779 §C](../rfc/rfc3779.txt), [3779 §3.2.3.4](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.4)))
- *the worked encodings in RFC 3779 §2.1 and §2.2.3:* addresses and prefixes (RFC [3779 §2.1.1](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.1.1)))
- *the worked encodings in RFC 3779 §2.1 and §2.2.3:* the all-addresses prefix and significant trailing zeros (RFC [3779 §2.1.2](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.1.2)))
  0/0 is a BIT STRING with no bits (03 01 00), and trailing zero bits are significant.
- *the worked encodings in RFC 3779 §2.1 and §2.2.3:* ranges expand min with zeros and max with ones (RFC [3779 §2.1.2](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.1.2)), [3779 §2.2.3.9](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.9)))
  Range ends: unspecified min bits are 0, unspecified max bits are 1.
- *the worked encodings in RFC 3779 §2.1 and §2.2.3:* the §2.2.3.8 prefix 128/4 covers 128.0.0.0 to 143.255.255.255 (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.8](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.8)))
- *edge cases:* ::/0, a single IPv6 address and the IPv4 /32 maximum
- *edge cases:* a prefix longer than the address family is an error
- *edge cases:* an unknown AFI keeps its bit strings undecoded
- *edge cases:* a range maximum with no one bits is accepted (erratum 2537) (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.9](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.9)))
  Verified erratum 2537 deleted the rule that a range maximum must contain
  a one bit. A maximum like 0.0.0.255 encodes as 24 zero bits (03 04 00
  00 00 00) and must be accepted.
- *edge cases:* malformed DER is an error
- *canonical form (reported, not enforced):* reports unsorted, overlapping and contiguous blocks (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.6](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.6)))
- *canonical form (reported, not enforced):* reports ranges that should be prefixes, non-minimal ends and inverted ranges (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.7](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.7)), [3779 §2.2.3.9](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.9)))
- *canonical form (reported, not enforced):* reports address families out of order or duplicated (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.3)))
- *canonical form (reported, not enforced):* reports AS identifiers that are unsorted, overlapping, contiguous or badly formed ranges (RFC [3779 §3.2.3.4](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.4)), [3779 §3.2.3.8](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.8)))
  Equal range ends are reported per erratum 7653, held for document update.
- *Barry fixture:* the m0-minimal-valid certificates carry Barry's default resources (RFC [3779 §2.2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3)), [3779 §3.2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3)))
  Barry's README: the TA holds everything, and the first CA gets 1/8, 0100::/8 and AS 0x01000000-0x01FFFFFF.

### `Lumina.ROATest`

[test/lumina/roa_test.exs](../../test/lumina/roa_test.exs)

Tests decoding of ROAs (RFC 9582). VRP output (M7) is built from these
structs, so the AS, prefixes and maxLength must decode exactly, from both
the RFC's own example (Appendix A, read from the RFC text) and Barry
objects. The RFC 9582 §4.3 encoding recommendations are reported by
issues/1, not enforced.

- *RFC 9582 Appendix A:* the example eContent decodes to AS65536 and 2001:db8::/32 (RFC [9582 §A](../rfc/rfc9582.txt))
- *RFC 9582 Appendix A:* the complete example object matches its stated size and digest, and decodes (RFC [9582 §A](../rfc/rfc9582.txt))
  The Base64 is read from the RFC text itself; the size and SHA-256 the RFC
  states prove the transcription is exact before anything is decoded.
- *Barry ROAs:* the m0-minimal-valid ROA authorizes AS1234 for its EE certificate's prefixes (RFC [9582 §4.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.2)), [9582 §4.3](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3)))
- *Barry ROAs:* IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes with and without maxLength (RFC [9582 §4.3.2.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.1)), [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
  An absent maxLength stays nil; the VRP then uses the prefix length.
- *Barry ROAs:* a ROA with version 2 decodes with version 2 (RFC [9582 §4.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.1)))
- *issues/1 (reported, not enforced):* maxLength below the prefix length, or equal to it, is reported (RFC [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
- *issues/1 (reported, not enforced):* maxLength above the address width is a decode error (RFC [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
  The module bounds maxLength by the family's address width (INTEGER (0..ub),
  ub = 32 or 128 via the information object set), so a maxLength above it
  fails at decode time rather than in issues/1 (F-012).
- *issues/1 (reported, not enforced):* IPv4-mapped IPv6 prefixes and repeated address families (RFC [9582 §4.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.1)))
- *issues/1 (reported, not enforced):* elements out of canonical order, and duplicates (RFC [9582 §4.3.3](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.3)), [9582 §4.3.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.3.1)))
- *errors:* a signed object that isn't a ROA
- *errors:* non-DER and unparseable eContent
- *errors:* an address family other than IPv4 or IPv6 is a decode error (RFC [9582 §4.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.1)))
  The module's information object set rejects other AFIs at decode time (F-012).

### `Lumina.ROAValidationTest`

[test/lumina/roa_validation_test.exs](../../test/lumina/roa_validation_test.exs)

Tests ROA content validation (#171): `Lumina.ROA.check/2` against the
ROA's EE certificate, RFC 9582 §4 and §5, and its use by `lumina
validate`.

§5 lists what a relying party checks beyond RFC 6488: the EE
certificate has the IP address delegation extension, without
`inherit`, and no AS identifier extension; every ROA prefix is within
the EE certificate's addresses; and the content conforms to §3 and §4.
"If any of the above checks fail, the ROA in its entirety MUST be
considered invalid." The §4.3 SHOULDs (a superfluous maxLength, order
and duplicates) only warn (D-030, F-018).

Most cases are in memory: the ROA and the EE certificate of
m0-minimal-valid's roa1.roa (EE 1.1.0.0/16 and 101::/16), changed one
field at a time, since Barry can't write some of them (an AS extension
on a ROA's EE certificate, two families with the same AFI, an
IPv4-mapped prefix). The `m7-roa-*` fixtures cover the rest end to end.

- *ROA.check/2:* a ROA whose prefixes are exactly its EE certificate's addresses has no problems (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)), [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
- *ROA.check/2:* prefixes strictly inside the EE certificate's addresses, with maxLength, are valid (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
- *ROA.check/2:* a version other than 0 is an error (RFC [9582 §4.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.1)))
- *ROA.check/2:* an EE certificate without the IP address delegation extension is an error (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
- *ROA.check/2:* an EE certificate that uses inherit for an address family is an error (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
- *ROA.check/2:* an EE certificate with the AS identifier delegation extension is an error (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
  Barry can't add the AS extension to a ROA's EE certificate, so this is in memory.
- *ROA.check/2:* a prefix outside the EE certificate's addresses is an error naming it (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
- *ROA.check/2:* a prefix that only partly overlaps the EE certificate's addresses is outside (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
  One address past the end: 1.1.0.0/15 covers 1.0.0.0/16 too.
- *ROA.check/2:* a prefix in a family the EE certificate doesn't list is outside (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
- *ROA.check/2:* a maxLength below the prefix length is an error (RFC [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
- *ROA.check/2:* two ROAIPAddressFamily elements with the same AFI are an error (RFC [9582 §4.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.1)))
- *ROA.check/2:* an IPv4-mapped IPv6 prefix is an error (RFC [9582 §4.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.1)))
- *ROA.check/2:* a maxLength equal to the prefix length only warns (RFC [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
- *ROA.check/2:* prefixes out of canonical order, or repeated, only warn (RFC [9582 §4.3.3](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.3)), [9582 §4.3.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.3.1)))
- *decoding:* an address family other than IPv4 or IPv6 is reported with the rule it breaks (RFC [9582 §4.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.1)))
  The ASN.1 module's information object set makes the decoder reject
  AFI 0003 (F-012); the error names the rule instead of a generic
  ASN.1 failure.
- *lumina validate:* an invalid ROA is listed with its rule, and the other ROAs at the point stay valid (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
  m7-roa-prefix-outside-ee: roa1.roa lists 1.2.0.0/16 outside its EE
  certificate; roa2.roa, in the same publication point, is fine.
- *lumina validate:* a ROA breaking only a SHOULD is valid, with a warning (RFC [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
  m7-roa-max-length-superfluous: a SHOULD, so a warning on a valid ROA (D-030).

### `Lumina.RsyncTest`

[test/lumina/rsync_test.exs](../../test/lumina/rsync_test.exs)

Tests the rsync runner (`Lumina.Rsync`, #72) against a real
`rsync --daemon` (`Lumina.Test.RsyncDaemon`) serving Barry fixture trees
and hand-made directories on 127.0.0.1. These tests are tagged `:rsync`
and excluded when no rsync 3.1.0 or later is installed.

They pin what the cache depends on: a publication point is fetched
recursively and byte-identical (D-009), files the server no longer has
are deleted, symlinks on the server never arrive, an oversize file is
skipped and reported rather than failing the fetch (D-008), and each
kind of failure gives its typed reason. A repository URI can never be
read as an rsync option.

- *fetching:* a publication point is fetched recursively and byte-identical (RFC [5781 §2](../rfc/rfc5781.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5781.html#section-2)), [6481 §3](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-3)))
  The whole publication point, subdirectories included, byte for byte (D-009).
- *fetching:* a nested publication point brings only its own subtree (RFC [6481 §2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2)))
- *fetching:* files the server no longer has are deleted from the destination
  An object withdrawn from the repository must not survive in the fetched copy.
- *fetching:* a previous copy given as :link_dest is reused for unchanged files
  With :link_dest, unchanged files are hard links to the previous copy, not new downloads.
- *fetching:* a single file, such as a TA certificate, is fetched to a path (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
- *untrusted servers:* symlinks on the server are not created locally
- *untrusted servers:* a file over the size limit is skipped and reported, and the rest is fetched
  D-008: an object over the size limit is skipped and reported; the rest
  of the publication point is still fetched. Failing the whole fetch
  would let one oversize file freeze the publication point.
- *untrusted servers:* a URI path that looks like an rsync option is only a path
  F-025: the rsync daemon reads a path starting with "-" as its own
  option. With the ./ the runner inserts, --help is just a missing file.
- *untrusted servers:* directories and files whose names start with - are fetched
  Base64url names can start with "-"; such directories and files must still fetch.
- *untrusted servers:* a URI with no module can't be fetched
- *failures:* a refused connection is :connection_refused
- *failures:* a host that doesn't resolve is :unknown_host
- *failures:* a module the server doesn't have is :no_such_module
- *failures:* a path the module doesn't have is :not_found
- *failures:* a server that never answers times out
  A server that accepts the connection and then says nothing hits the I/O timeout (D-008).
- *the rsync binary:* check finds rsync 3.1.0 or later
- *the rsync binary:* a missing binary is :rsync_not_found, for check and for a fetch
- *the rsync binary:* an rsync older than 3.1.0 is rejected

### `Lumina.SignedObjectTest`

[test/lumina/signed_object_test.exs](../../test/lumina/signed_object_test.exs)

Tests decoding of the CMS SignedData envelope shared by all RPKI signed
objects (RFC 6488, RFC 5652). Signature checks (M5) need the exact signed
attributes and the EE certificate, and the ROA and manifest decoders need
the eContent, so the envelope must expose all of them faithfully.
Profile violations decode; only non-DER or unparseable input fails.

- *the m0-minimal-valid signed objects:* decode into SignedData with one EE certificate and the eContent type named (RFC [6488 §2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2)), [6488 §2.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1)), [6488 §2.1.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.1)), [6488 §2.1.3.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.3.1)), [6488 §2.1.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.4)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid signed objects:* the EE certificate is decoded from the object's bytes, and the signer ID is its SKI (RFC [6488 §2.1.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.4)), [6488 §2.1.6.2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.2)))
  The EE certificate keeps the exact bytes from the object; the signer is named by its SKI.
- *the m0-minimal-valid signed objects:* the signed attributes decode: content type, message digest and signing time (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4)), [6488 §2.1.6.4.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4.1)), [6488 §2.1.6.4.2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4.2)), [6488 §2.1.6.4.3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4.3)), [9589 §4](../rfc/rfc9589.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9589.html#section-4)))
  Decode sanity only: content-type matches eContentType and message-digest is SHA-256 of eContent.
- *the m0-minimal-valid signed objects:* signed_attrs_der is the object's signedAttrs bytes, re-tagged as a SET OF (RFC [5652 §5.4](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-5.4)), [6488 §2.1.6.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4)))
  The signature covers the DER of signedAttrs as a SET OF (tag 0x31), not
  the [0] IMPLICIT form in the object. Checked structurally here; the
  signature itself is verified in M5.
- *the m0-minimal-valid signed objects:* the signer's algorithms and signature (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.3)), [6488 §2.1.6.5](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.5)), [6488 §2.1.6.6](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.6)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
- *content types:* decode_econtent/1 decodes ROA and manifest eContent with their ASN.1 types (RFC [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9286 §4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4)))
- *content types:* the content types not decoded until M9 are named but have no decoder
- *content types:* an unknown eContent type decodes the envelope and leaves eContent raw
  An unknown eContent type is not a decoding error; the envelope decodes and eContent stays raw.
- *structural decoding:* a forbidden signed attribute decodes and is named (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4)), [9589 §4](../rfc/rfc9589.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9589.html#section-4)))
  RFC 9589 removed binary-signing-time; it must still decode so M5 can name it.
- *structural decoding:* a ContentInfo that isn't SignedData is an error (RFC [6488 §2.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1)), [5652 §5.1](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-5.1)))
- *structural decoding:* an embedded certificate that doesn't decode is an error naming the certificate
- *structural decoding:* signed attributes out of DER order are rejected as not canonical (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
  signedAttrs is an [0] IMPLICIT SET OF, so a schema-less DER walk can't
  see its order (X.690 11.6). Only re-encoding catches unsorted
  attributes, and the signature covers these exact bytes.
- *structural decoding:* non-DER, truncated and unrelated input are errors naming the layer

### `Lumina.SyncSharedModulesTest`

[test/lumina/sync_shared_modules_test.exs](../../test/lumina/sync_shared_modules_test.exs)

Tests that one sync fetches a module once, however many TALs' trees
reach it (#102, D-012).

`Lumina.Sync.run/3` walks each TAL's tree in turn and passes the
modules each walk fetched (or failed to fetch) to the next, so a module
shared by several trees, such as a hosted repository serving CAs under
several RIRs, costs one rsync run per sync, and a module that failed
isn't retried. Each tree is still walked whole.

The two "trees" here are one Barry fixture, m0-minimal-valid, served by
a local rsync daemon, under two TAL names: everything below the TA is
in the shared module `rsync://localhost:8873/rpki`.

- a module two TALs' trees share is fetched once, and both trees are walked
- a shared module that failed isn't fetched again for the next TAL
  After a first sync, the shared module's host is remapped to a closed
  port: the first walk's fetch fails and its copy goes stale; the
  second walk doesn't try again and reads the same stale copy.
- the summary says which modules an earlier TAL's walk fetched

### `Lumina.TATest`

[test/lumina/ta_test.exs](../../test/lumina/ta_test.exs)

Tests TA retrieval (`Lumina.TA`, #74): the TAL's URIs tried in D-003
order over the real fetchers, each certificate checked against the TAL
(RFC 8630 §3), the next URI tried on any failure, the accepted
certificate kept in the cache, and the previous one offered as stale
when every URI fails.

HTTPS URIs are served by `Lumina.Test.HTTPSServer` with a CA made in the
test, rsync URIs by `Lumina.Test.RsyncDaemon`, both serving Barry
fixture TAs. The fixture TALs name fixed ports, so each test points the
TAL at its own servers by replacing its URIs; the key stays the
fixture's.

- *retrieval:* every Barry fixture's TA is retrieved over rsync and stored byte-identical (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)))
  Fixtures whose TA is expected invalid (m2-ta-*, m4-chain-ta-*) are
  covered by the next tests.
- *retrieval:* a fixture TA that fails the TAL check is fetched but not accepted (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
- *retrieval:* a TA whose self-signature fails, or that has expired, is fetched but not accepted (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  D-014: TAL checks alone (M2) would accept both; validation rejects them.
- *retrieval:* when the first URI is unreachable, the next one is used (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
- *retrieval:* a certificate whose key doesn't match is reported, and the next URI is used (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)))
- *retrieval:* content that isn't a certificate is reported, and the next URI is used
- *retrieval:* an HTTPS URI is tried before an rsync URI listed ahead of it (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
  D-003: HTTPS first, whatever the TAL order. The rsync URI is never tried.
- *the cache:* when every URI fails, the error lists each attempt and the previous TA is kept (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [8897 §7](../rfc/rfc8897.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8897.html#section-7)))
  The last accepted TA is kept, byte for byte, and offered as stale with its source.
- *the cache:* a previously accepted TA that has since expired is not offered as stale (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
- *the cache:* when every URI fails and nothing was cached, there is no stale TA
- *the cache:* a rejected certificate never replaces the accepted one
  A TA rejected later must not replace the one accepted before.
- *the cache:* each URI's outcome is recorded in the cache status

### `Lumina.TALCheckTest`

[test/lumina/tal_check_test.exs](../../test/lumina/tal_check_test.exs)

Tests checking a trust anchor certificate against its TAL (RFC 8630
§2.3, §3; #56). Everything the validator trusts hangs off the TA, so a
certificate must be refused if its key isn't the TAL's, if it isn't a
self-signed CA, or if its resources are missing, empty or inherited.
Signature and validity checks are M4.

- every Barry TA passes against its own TAL, except the ones built to fail (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)), [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
- the TA fixtures built to fail give exactly their problem (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)), [3779 §2.2.3.5](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.5)), [6487 §4.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.1)))
- a TA certificate whose key isn't the TAL's is rejected (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)), [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
  Two well-formed TAs from different fixtures: only the key ties a certificate to its TAL.
- a CA certificate that isn't self-issued can't be a TA, even with a matching TAL (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)), [6487 §4.8.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.3)))
- an EE certificate can't be a TA (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)), [6487 §4.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.1)))
- *resources:* an inherited AS number set is rejected (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)))
- *resources:* an AS extension with no identifiers is rejected (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)))
  Each present resource extension must hold resources (F-023); an empty AS extension fails even with IP resources.
- *resources:* a TA with no resource extensions at all is rejected (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)), [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)), [6487 §4.8.11](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.11)))
- *resources:* a resource extension that doesn't decode is reported, not ignored
- each problem names its rule, RFC section and reason

### `Lumina.TALRealRepoTest`

[test/lumina/tal_realrepo_test.exs](../../test/lumina/tal_realrepo_test.exs)

Checks the LACNIC TAL against the LACNIC TA certificate in the
maintainer's local copy of the LACNIC repository, `test/realrepos/`
(#58). That copy is git-ignored and only current until its objects
expire. These tests are tagged `:realrepo` and excluded when the copy
isn't present (`test/test_helper.exs`). `check_ta/2` doesn't look at
validity dates (M4), so the check stays meaningful after expiry.

- the LACNIC TA certificate matches the LACNIC TAL (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)))
  The real LACNIC TA certificate, fetched by rsync, matches LACNIC's published TAL.
- the LACNIC TA certificate doesn't match the ARIN TAL (RFC [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)))
  A real TA certificate against another RIR's TAL: the key check must catch it.

### `Lumina.TALRIRTest`

[test/lumina/tal_rir_test.exs](../../test/lumina/tal_rir_test.exs)

Real-world TALs: the five RIRs' published TALs in
`test/fixtures/tals/rir/` (#58), byte-exact copies approved by the
maintainer. Each must parse under the strict grammar (D-002) with no
warnings, list the URIs the RIR published, and carry an RSA 2048-bit key
(RFC 7935 §3). The Subject Key Identifier pins the key itself: if an RIR
rolls its key, refreshing the file fails here until the change is
reviewed. The SHA-256 in the README must match each file, so the
recorded provenance stays true.

- the AFRINIC TAL parses cleanly, with its published URIs and an RSA 2048 key (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
  AFRINIC's TAL lists rsync first; D-003 still tries HTTPS first.
- the APNIC TAL parses cleanly, with its published URIs and an RSA 2048 key (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
  The HTTPS-first variant from APNIC's TAL archive (maintainer's choice; the current apnic.tal is rsync only).
- the ARIN TAL parses cleanly, with its published URIs and an RSA 2048 key (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
  ARIN's TAL starts with an 11-line disclaimer, so it exercises the comment rules on a real file.
- the LACNIC TAL parses cleanly, with its published URIs and an RSA 2048 key (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
  LACNIC's TAL has no final newline, which RFC 8630 §2.2 doesn't require.
- the RIPE NCC TAL parses cleanly, with its published URIs and an RSA 2048 key (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
  RIPE NCC's preferred TAL file.
- all five RIR TALs carry RSA 2048-bit keys (RFC [7935 §3](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-3)))
- every TAL in the folder is listed in the README with its SHA-256
  The README records each file's source and SHA-256; a changed file must update it.

### `Lumina.TALTest`

[test/lumina/tal_test.exs](../../test/lumina/tal_test.exs)

Tests the TAL parser (RFC 8630 §2.2, strict grammar per D-002). The test
TAL corpus (#55) fixes the exact outcome, rule and line for every case.
Barry's TALs must parse, and must carry exactly their TA certificate's
key, because everything the validator trusts starts from this key.

- every case in the test TAL corpus gives exactly its expected outcome (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [8630 §2.4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.4)), [4648 §4](../rfc/rfc4648.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4648.html#section-4)), [3986 §3](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3)))
  The corpus states each case's expected outcome; any difference, including the line, fails.
- every Barry TAL parses and carries its TA certificate's key (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [8630 §2.3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.3)))
  Barry writes one TAL per repository; its key must be exactly the TA certificate's SPKI.
- the RFC 8630 example parses into its comments, two URIs and an RSA 2048 key (RFC [8630 §2.4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.4)), [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
- CRLF and LF line ends give the same result (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
- trailing whitespace is ignored and warned about, giving the same TAL (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
  D-002: trailing whitespace is ignored, with one warning per line.
- errors carry a line, a rule, an RFC reference and a message
- a missing file is an error

### `Lumina.TALURIOrderTest`

[test/lumina/tal_uri_order_test.exs](../../test/lumina/tal_uri_order_test.exs)

Tests the order in which a TAL's URIs are tried (D-003, #57): HTTPS first
in TAL order, then rsync in TAL order. RFC 8630 §3 leaves the rule to each
relying party and §4 recommends HTTPS; the fetcher in M3 follows this
order and moves to the next URI on failure or key mismatch.

- HTTPS URIs come before rsync URIs, whatever their order in the TAL (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [8630 §4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-4)))
- TAL order is kept within each scheme (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)))
  Within a scheme the TAL's own order is the operator's preference, so it is kept.
- a TAL with a single scheme keeps its order
- scheme case doesn't matter (RFC [3986 §3.1](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3.1)))
  Schemes are case-insensitive, so HTTPS:// counts as HTTPS.
- the RFC 8630 example and every Barry TAL list HTTPS first (RFC [8630 §3](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-3)), [8630 §2.4](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.4)))

### `Lumina.URITest`

[test/lumina/uri_test.exs](../../test/lumina/uri_test.exs)

Tests repository URI parsing, normalization and cache-path mapping
(`Lumina.URI`, #70). URIs come from certificates anyone can publish and
become paths on disk, so besides the normalization rules (RFC 3986 §6.2)
the tests pin every rejection rule, and check over a corpus of hostile
inputs that no accepted URI maps outside the cache root. Real URIs, from
Barry fixtures and the RIR TALs, must parse and map as expected.

- *normalization:* scheme and host are lowercased; the path keeps its case (RFC [3986 §6.2.2.1](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-6.2.2.1)))
- *normalization:* the default port and an empty port are dropped; other ports are kept (RFC [3986 §6.2.3](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-6.2.3)), [5781 §2](../rfc/rfc5781.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5781.html#section-2)))
- *normalization:* a trailing slash doesn't change the URI, its module or its cache path (RFC [6487 §4.8.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.1)), [6481 §2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2)))
  F-016: no RFC says whether a caRepository URI ends in "/". Both forms
  must name the same directory, module and cache path (#43).
- *normalization:* IPv6 literals are accepted, lowercased, with or without a port (RFC [3986 §3.2.2](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3.2.2)))
- *rejection rules:* only rsync and https are accepted (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
- *rejection rules:* user information is rejected (RFC [3986 §7.5](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-7.5)))
  RFC 5781 allows user@ in rsync URIs; RPKI repositories are public, so Lumina doesn't.
- *rejection rules:* an empty, malformed or non-ASCII host is rejected (RFC [3986 §3.2.2](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3.2.2)))
- *rejection rules:* a port outside 1-65535 or with non-digits is rejected (RFC [3986 §3.2.3](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3.2.3)))
- *rejection rules:* queries and fragments are rejected (RFC [3986 §3.4](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3.4)), [3986 §3.5](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3.5)))
- *rejection rules:* dot segments and empty segments are rejected (RFC [3986 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3.3)), [3986 §6.2.2.3](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-6.2.2.3)))
  Dot segments are rejected, not resolved: resolving them is how a URI escapes the cache.
- *rejection rules:* percent-encoding is rejected (RFC [3986 §2.1](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-2.1)), [5781 §2](../rfc/rfc5781.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5781.html#section-2)))
  Decoding percent-encoding would give one file two spellings, and %2F or %2E%2E a way out.
- *rejection rules:* characters outside pchar are rejected (RFC [3986 §3.3](../rfc/rfc3986.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986.html#section-3.3)))
- *rejection rules:* every error names its rule, RFC section and reason
- *modules:* an rsync URI's module is its first path segment (RFC [5781 §2](../rfc/rfc5781.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5781.html#section-2)))
- *modules:* an rsync URI with no path, and an https URI, have no module
- *cache paths:* a URI maps to <root>/<scheme>/<host[:port]>/<path>
- *cache paths:* rsync and https copies of the same host and path don't share a cache path
- *cache paths:* no accepted URI maps outside the cache root
  Every combination of a hostile host and a hostile path is either
  rejected or maps strictly inside the cache root, and a rejected one
  always names a rule.
- *real URIs:* every URI in every RIR TAL parses, and its text is already normal (RFC [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)))
- *real URIs:* every Barry TAL's rsync URI is in module rpki on localhost:8873 (RFC [5781 §2](../rfc/rfc5781.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5781.html#section-2)))

### `Lumina.VRPCollectionTest`

[test/lumina/vrp_collection_test.exs](../../test/lumina/vrp_collection_test.exs)

Tests collecting VRPs in `Lumina.Validate.run/3` (#164): the VRPs of
the valid ROAs, each with the trust anchor's name (D-032) and the URI
of the ROA it comes from, in a fixed order (IPv4 first, then address,
prefix length, maxLength, AS, trust anchor, URI).

RFC 9582 §4.3.2.2: without maxLength, "the AS is only authorized to
advertise the exact prefix", so the VRP's maxLength is the prefix
length. §5: an invalid ROA "in its entirety" gives nothing. Duplicates
are kept here, one per ROA; the default output lists a VRP once
(D-033).

Each test syncs a Barry fixture from a local rsync daemon and validates
the cache at 2030-01-01.

- *Validate.run/3:* a fixture's VRPs are those its valid ROAs state, in order, with trust anchor and URI (RFC [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)), [9582 §4.3.2.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.1)))
  m1-roa-prefixes: AS64496 with 1.1.0.0/17-24, 1.1.128.0/24 and
  0101::/16-48, IPv4 first and in address order.
- *Validate.run/3:* a prefix without maxLength gives a VRP whose maxLength is the prefix length (RFC [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
  m1-roa-prefixes' 1.1.128.0/24 has no maxLength: the VRP's is 24.
- *Validate.run/3:* an invalid ROA contributes no VRPs, and the other ROAs at the point still do (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
  m7-roa-prefix-outside-ee: roa1.roa is invalid (a prefix outside its
  EE certificate), so none of its prefixes count, not even 1.1.0.0/16,
  which is inside; roa2.roa's do.
- *Validate.run/3:* two ROAs stating the same VRP both appear, each with its URI (RFC [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
  m7-vrp-duplicate: both ROAs authorize AS64496 for 1.1.0.0/16 (D-033).
- *Validate.run/3:* a ROA served from its point's last valid copy contributes its VRPs (RFC [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)), [9582 §5](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-5)))
  A copy of m0-minimal-valid: after a first sync, a newer manifest
  number is recorded for ca1, so the live point is a replay
  (manifest_number_replay, D-024) and its last valid copy stands in
  (D-023). The ROA there is valid and its VRPs count.
- the trust anchor's name is the TAL file's name without .tal (D-032)

### `Lumina.VRPCompareTest`

[test/lumina/vrp_compare_test.exs](../../test/lumina/vrp_compare_test.exs)

Tests comparing Lumina's VRPs with a reference CSV (#168, D-035):
`Lumina.VRPCompare` and `mix lumina.compare_vrps`.

The reference is Routinator's published CSV, in the columns `lumina
vrps` writes (D-032). Both sides are compared per trust anchor as sets
of VRPs, Lumina's trust anchor names mapped to the reference's; lines
that aren't VRPs are reported, not fatal. Small CSVs written here cover
the cases; the `:network` test downloads the live file.

- *compare/2:* identical CSVs have no differences
- *compare/2:* a VRP only one side has is listed under that side
- *compare/2:* a trust anchor only one side has is reported as missing from the other
  Lumina validated only LACNIC; the reference has every trust anchor.
- *compare/2:* Lumina's trust anchor names are mapped to the reference's
  Lumina names trust anchors after its TAL files (D-032).
- *compare/2:* VRPs are compared by value, not by text, and duplicates count once
  2001:DB8:0:0::/32 and 2001:db8::/32 are the same prefix; a repeated row counts once.
- *parse/1:* a malformed line is reported with its number and skipped
- *parse/1:* a CSV without the header is an error
- *parse/1:* quoted fields and lumina vrps --wide output are read
  Lumina.VRP quotes a field holding a comma or quote; --wide adds a URI column.
- *report/2:* lists at most limit VRPs per side, and how many more
- *mix lumina.compare_vrps:* compares two files and reports both sides' malformed lines
- the live reference CSV downloads and parses, with every RIR's trust anchor
  Downloads Routinator's CSV; about 34 MB and over a million VRPs (2026-11-15).

### `Lumina.WalkTest`

[test/lumina/walk_test.exs](../../test/lumina/walk_test.exs)

Tests the repository walk (`Lumina.Walk`, #75) against real rsync
daemons serving Barry fixtures: from the TA, every publication point
reached through CA certificates is mirrored into the cache (RFC 6481 §5).
The unit of fetching is the rsync module of a publication point, fetched
at most once per run; publication points in a module already fetched
are read from that copy (D-012).

The `m3-walk-*` fixtures each exercise one part of the walk: a
delegation to a second rsync host, a nested publication point, an SIA
loop, a deep chain, an unreachable host and CAs in separate modules of
one host. The walk follows only CAs that validate (D-014, #113): the
`m4-chain-*` fixtures show what isn't followed. The fixtures name `localhost:8873` (and `other.example:8873`),
so each test remaps those to its own daemons with `:remap`; cache paths
and reports keep the names from the certificates.

- *mirroring:* every Barry fixture mirrors completely from the local daemon (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [6481 §2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2)))
  Each module a fixture serves on localhost:8873 must arrive byte for
  byte. Fixtures that need a second host, or that are built to be
  unreachable, have their own tests; so do the m2-ta-* fixtures,
  whose TA is never accepted.
- *mirroring:* publication points in sibling directories of one module take one rsync run (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [5781 §2](../rfc/rfc5781.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5781.html#section-2)))
  D-012: the TA's and ca1's publication points are sibling
  directories of module rpki. Under D-009 they took two runs; the
  module takes one.
- *mirroring:* a CA whose publication point is on a second rsync host is fetched there (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [6487 §4.8.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.1)))
  Like LACNIC's delegations to registro.br and Amazon, fetched where the certificate says.
- *mirroring:* a publication point nested in one already fetched causes no extra rsync run (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  The fetch of the TA's module already brought ca1's directory; one rsync run in all.
- *mirroring:* each fetch's outcome is recorded in the cache status
- *limits (D-008):* an SIA loop terminates, with the loop reported (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
- *limits (D-008):* a chain deeper than the limit stops there, reported (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  RFC 6481 §5's locally configured maximum chain length, set to 2
  here: ca3 is depth 3. Its files arrive with the module, but it isn't
  walked.
- *limits (D-008):* the default depth limit lets a five-level chain through
- *failures:* a child CA on an unreachable host is reported, and the rest is mirrored (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
- *failures:* an unreachable publication point keeps its last good copy, walked as stale (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [8897 §7](../rfc/rfc8897.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8897.html#section-7)))
  First run: the host is reachable (remapped to a daemon). Second run:
  it isn't. The last good copy stays byte-identical, and the walk
  continues from it, marked stale.
- *concurrent fetches (D-011):* modules on one host are fetched at most :per_host at a time (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  Eight modules on one host, fetched in one level. The daemon refuses
  a third connection, so a single refusal would show the cap was
  exceeded.
- *concurrent fetches (D-011):* modules on one host are fetched concurrently
  The converse of the test above: with :per_host above what the daemon
  accepts, it refuses some of the eight module fetches, which shows
  they really run at the same time.
- *concurrent fetches (D-011):* points and fetches are reported in walk order, whatever order the fetches finish in (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  The order a sequential walk gives: the TA's module first, then s1 to s8 as listed.
- *not waiting for a slow host (#88):* a deep branch is walked while a silent host's fetch is still waiting (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  m3-walk-silent-branch: ca1's host accepts connections and never
  answers (rsync's connect timeout covers only the TCP connection,
  so the I/O timeout ends that fetch: both 5 s here); ca2, ca3 and ca4 each need a
  fetch, one level after the other. Each point is validated as soon
  as its module is in and its children's modules are fetched right
  away, so ca4's module arrives while ca1's fetch is still waiting.
  Points, fetches and issues are still reported in walk order.
- *validation (D-014):* every positive Barry fixture walks without an invalid CA (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  Same points as M3 gave: no CA of a positive fixture is reported
  invalid. Warnings are allowed (m4-cert-unknown-extension, D-013).
- *validation (D-014):* a CA that doesn't validate is reported with its reasons, and nothing below it is walked (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  ca1's directory arrives with the module (D-012), but it isn't walked.
- *validation (D-014):* a revoked CA isn't walked, and its sibling is (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)))
- *validation (D-014):* a CRL that is missing fails the publication point, and nothing below is walked (RFC [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)), [9829 §3.2](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.2)), [9286 §6.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.2)))
  The TA's manifest names the missing CRL too, so the TA's point fails (#134).
- *validation (D-014):* a TA certificate published in its own publication point is ignored (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)))
  #103: LACNIC publishes its TA certificate in the TA's own
  publication point. It isn't on the TA's manifest, so it isn't
  used (#134): no loop, no invalid CA.
- *validation (D-014):* a certificate not on the manifest is ignored, not walked or reported (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [9286 §6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6)))
  A CA certificate from another fixture, in ta/ but not on the TA's
  manifest: files not on the manifest "MUST NOT be used" (#134).
- *validation (D-014):* a certificate naming the CA as issuer but with another AKI is reported invalid (RFC [6487 §4.8.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.3)), [6487 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-7.2)))
  Only one of the two names another CA: a fault, reported.
- *validation (D-014):* a CA certificate without Basic Constraints is reported invalid, not skipped (RFC [6487 §4.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.1)), [6487 §4.8.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.4)))
  Its Key Usage has keyCertSign, so it is checked as a CA and the
  missing Basic Constraints reported (#115); it isn't walked.
- *publication points (RFC 9286 §6, #134):* a publication point that fails is reported, and nothing below it is walked (RFC [9286 §6.5](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.5)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
  ca1's manifest lists roa1.roa with a wrong hash: the point fails, the walk goes on elsewhere.
- *last valid copy (D-023, #135):* a point that fails is walked from its last valid copy, and nothing below disappears (RFC [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)), [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)))
  m3-walk-deep served from a copy. After a first walk, ca1's listed
  ca2.cer changes (its hash no longer matches): ca1's point falls
  back to the copy the first walk kept, and ca2, ca3 and ca4 are
  still walked from it.
- *caught mid-update (RFC 6481 §5, #137):* a point whose files don't match its manifest is fetched once more, and accepted (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [9286 §6.5](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.5)))
  The update finishes between the two fetches: the point is accepted after the retry.
- *caught mid-update (RFC 6481 §5, #137):* a point that stays inconsistent fails after exactly one retry (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [9286 §6.5](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.5)), [9286 §6.6](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.6)))
- *caught mid-update (RFC 6481 §5, #137):* a sibling in a module refetched in the same level is validated against the new copy (RFC [6481 §5](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-5)), [9286 §6.5](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-6.5)))
  m3-walk-shared-module: ca2 and ca3 are siblings in one module,
  both caught mid-update. A level's points are validated in parallel
  before they are reported (#169); the refetch the first triggers
  repairs the second too, which must be validated again rather than
  keep its result from before the refetch.
